records.summary: Evaluate persisted review verdicts after reading required-review declarations
records.whyHappened: The explicit boolean adapter introduced a missing-review placeholder even when the report scanner had already indexed an approved report. The placeholder overrode the normal report verdict evaluator.
records.causalChain: needCodeReview true plus no explicit outcome row -> synthetic missing decision -> approved report attached only as a path -> false blocking gate.
records.testGap: Boolean combination tests lacked indexed reports. Report tests lacked the new boolean declaration block.
records.missingDecision: A required-review flag declares an obligation, not a failed or missing verdict. When a report is indexed, the existing report evaluator decides approval or unresolved findings. Explicit execution failures, unknown report verdicts, canonical records and review requirements remain enforced.

records.summary: Honor explicit independent phase flags and classify health outcomes as optional warnings
records.whyHappened: The compatibility scanner ignored the Phase Gate Declarations JSON and read older Required execution prose as a coverage obligation. The shared blocker predicate treated all unknown or missing outcomes identically, so health metadata and health failures blocked acceptance.
records.causalChain: Repair preserves explicit false flags but legacy projection ignores them -> tests missing; unrecognized health prose -> unknown -> blocker; failed supporting lint mapping could additionally manufacture a behavioral coverage failure.
records.testGap: Tests covered canonical gate JSON and older Markdown tables separately, without scanning boolean declarations through repair evidence. Health tests assumed blocking semantics instead of distinguishing optional user-owned warning repair.
records.missingDecision: Portable explicit boolean declarations govern legacy applicability. Canonical gate records and native execution results remain authoritative; configured test failures still require resolution. Required coverage/review remain independent. Build/lint findings are visible warnings, not passes or blockers; they cannot invalidate an otherwise passing behavioral coverage mapping. A declared verification task with only health findings completes without automatic repair, preserving raw outcomes.

records.summary: Keep repair controls and artifact diagnostics with their declared phase owners
records.whyHappened: The readiness summary duplicated phase repair shortcuts and flattened all artifact diagnostics into feature-level errors, even when the validator provided an affected phase document.
records.causalChain: Owned phase issues -> global blocker list -> repetitive indistinguishable shortcuts and repeated path guidance obscure the actual repair owner.
records.testGap: Presentation tests asserted navigation shortcuts, but did not require phase-only controls or exact artifact-path attribution.
records.missingDecision: Resolve artifact ownership only from the declared document path. Display phase diagnostics and repair controls in the owning phase. Feature-level errors stay in readiness; manual verification messages stay beside manual controls. Placement changes do not waive gates, fabricate missing statuses or grant repair authority.

records.summary: Accept bound terminal console capture on unchanged static AND command lists
records.whyHappened: All selected checks passed but a static AND-list receipt added terminal log redirection; the capture matcher accepted only a simple command or whole-list grouping.
records.causalChain: Static checks succeed -> terminal command writes a checksum-bound audit log -> equivalent AND-list rejected -> coverage assessment cannot start.
records.testGap: Existing capture tests covered grouped AND lists and simple commands, not terminal capture on an unchanged non-test AND list.
records.missingDecision: Static/preparation/discovery AND-list terminal capture preserves command selection, control flow and exit status. Accept it without claiming earlier stdout is in that log. Native stdout test reports still require complete capture; changed commands and failures remain rejected.

records.summary: Expose failed Refresh checks to phase repair with historical-green investigation and fresh verification
records.whyHappened: Fresh receipt failures were projected only as an external blocker. Phase repair admission consulted historical phase gates and could reject repair even though the current configured checks had failed.
records.causalChain: Implementation reports green -> later Refresh executes a failing configured command -> external-only blocker hides repair -> phase action rejects historical satisfied gate -> user cannot request scoped remediation.
records.testGap: Tests covered missing phase evidence and Refresh failure independently, but not repairable bound failed commands associated with a previously green phase or the independent verification handoff after that repair.
records.missingDecision: Current failed execution facts and inspected ownership must supply generic phase recovery gaps. Reconcile before/after evidence and source history, repair within scope, validate actual outcomes independently, and preserve cancellation/human acceptance. No project or phase-specific route.

records.summary: Separate execution context from nonunique test display names
records.whyHappened: Native report import treated displayed file/method names as unique execution keys, rejecting valid parameterized cases and same-named tests from independent assemblies or reports.
records.causalChain: Configured tests execute successfully -> reporter preserves repeated labels -> global name uniqueness rejects valid evidence -> acceptance coverage assessment cannot start.
records.testGap: Existing native reporter tests covered unique names and duplicate execution records but not real parameterized runner output, distinct native executions sharing labels or independent assemblies sharing method names.
records.missingDecision: Validate native execution records and report bindings separately from labels. Keep every occurrence and its execution context without inventing stable TestPlan IDs, coverage mappings or passes. Duplicate reports, invalid native bindings and nonpassing/count-inconsistent outcomes remain rejected.

records.summary: Admit evidence-preserving console capture across check kinds and bound repository revisions
records.whyHappened: Receipt normalization admitted console capture only for tests with a separate native report, while workers also capture lint/build and native stdout. Multi-repository test execution records more than one legitimate revision.
records.causalChain: All checks execute -> receipt records cwd and captured logs -> static command falsely mismatches plan -> coverage assessment never starts; native stdout and multiple source revisions would fail at later entries.
records.testGap: Console-capture tests covered separate test reports but omitted static/preparation/discovery, grouped health commands, stdout-only native reports and explicitly bound linked source revisions.
records.missingDecision: Command presentation and audit capture must not depend on gate kind. Preserve exact selection/control flow, checksums, native outcomes and source bindings; reject forged evidence or unbound revision alternatives.

records.summary: Separate verification command cwd from configured source repository ownership
records.whyHappened: A configured package command delegated to a runner in a linked repository, but plan validation confined its configuration and tests to the command repository.
records.causalChain: Valid wrapper and linked test paths -> rejected inspection plan -> correction removed source references and investigated alternative test locations -> correction runtime exhausted before any test execution.
records.testGap: Prior multi-repository fixtures launched a command from each source owner; none exercised a wrapper command with all test sources in another repository.
records.missingDecision: Resolve source ownership from explicit configuration references, preserve execution cwd and command, confine selected source to the bound repositories, and include all source owners in freshness and overlap checks. Optional metadata and gate applicability remain independent.

records.summary: Resolve verified model aliases before runtime and prepare distinct tokenizer assets
records.whyHappened: A selectable current provider model ID was absent from the tokenizer map, while the request guard selected asset preparation with a separate version-name substring.
records.causalChain: Current catalogue alias -> unsupported local mapping -> worker launch then tokenizer failure before inspection or tests
records.testGap: Existing tests covered GPT text and unknown model rejection but not official model alias evolution, provider identity, asset verification or rejection before spawning.
records.missingDecision: A catalogue ID and verified tokenizer capability must agree; aliases map to independently verified versioned assets through one resolver used by preflight, readiness and worker preparation.

records.summary: Remove project and numbered-phase gate overrides across producers and readers
records.whyHappened: Generic JSON gates coexisted with numbered-phase recipe overrides, named-project prompt rules and legacy file-presence inference.
records.causalChain: Contradictory producers -> implicit gate changes or unnecessary execution -> phase-dependent admission and repair behavior
records.testGap: Tests verified the shared policy was included but did not reject contradictory recipe bodies; legacy fixtures assumed file lists implied passing tests.
records.missingDecision: Declarations and independently validated evidence are authoritative at every boundary. Supporting health evidence cannot invalidate a valid behavioral mapping. Missing declarations need reconciliation, not file-type inference.

records.summary: Separate acceptance coverage from numeric measurement at production and admission
records.whyHappened: A compatibility worker interpreted legacy numeric measurement N/A as needTestCoverage=false despite supplying an active acceptance assessment.
records.causalChain: Ambiguous boolean description and historical measurement wording -> incorrect applicability flag -> active assessment skipped by reducer despite passing execution
records.testGap: Four-flag tests used consistent outcomes and did not reproduce contradictory disabled flags with actual passing execution and populated acceptance mappings.
records.missingDecision: The flag controls meaningful acceptance coverage. Numeric policy absence cannot disable it. Reject structurally contradictory assessments independently of prose, preserve existing evidence, and reconcile within the same phase.

records.summary: Use independent structured phase gates and same-phase repair before escalation
records.whyHappened: Human report-count wording was used as gate authority and every unresolved projection stopped the workflow.
records.causalChain: Passing executions -> different prose -> unknown projection -> immediate workflow block
records.testGap: No shared boolean matrix exercised actual execution evidence through scanner, repair, SQLite and finalization.
records.missingDecision: Bind each phase to explicit gates and configured checks. Resolve ordinary failures in the same phase; reassess repeated lack of progress. Phase identifiers do not choose policy.

records.summary: Use consistent counted-check outcome grammar in legacy phase evidence
records.whyHappened: Row discovery recognized fixture suites but the passing-count parser only accepted bare counts or counts named tests. A passing fixture result became unknown and overrode green phase evidence.
records.causalChain: Worker executed passing verification and accepted its phase -> fixture-count noun rejected by legacy importer -> tests projected unknown -> next phase blocked.
records.testGap: Earlier fixtures changed suite labels but retained passed-count wording. No matrix varied both count nouns and outcomes or carried fixture-count results through continuation and finalization.
records.missingDecision: Counted verification units must share the same vocabulary in row discovery, positive execution and failure detection. Explicit failure, partial execution, zero execution, discovery-only commands and missing required coverage remain unresolved.

records.summary: Reconcile equivalent legacy execution records before phase and feature completion admission
records.whyHappened: Passing health and test results were recorded in supported human-readable tables, but admission required duplicate health rows and particular count wording. Valid evidence became missing or unknown after worker completion.
records.causalChain: Required declarations plus incomplete result import -> unknown/missing projection -> completed phase blocked before continuation or finalization.
records.testGap: Earlier tests exercised only one empty-target wording and per-suite passed counts, and did not cover health results in a separate metrics table through the real scanner/SQLite/finalization path.
records.missingDecision: Normalize equivalent legacy recorded results before applying the guard. Explicit failures, missing required coverage, unexecuted checks and invalid native JSON remain blocking. Normalization does not rerun tests, rewrite artifacts or invent new obligations.

records.summary: Carry shared acceptance ownership and test-to-code traceability from EPIC creation through tasks
records.whyHappened: Planning entry points lacked one durable distinction between isolated lower-level tests and complete EPIC workflow E2E. Flat gate reasoning risked imposing a browser test per phase or discarding higher-level workflow obligations.
records.causalChain: Missing acceptance ownership -> incompatible phase/feature/EPIC test assumptions -> duplicated E2E work or lost workflow evidence and difficult bug localization.
records.testGap: Generic tests exercise policy injection into EPIC creation/refinement, feature slicing and generated documents, phase/task planning and verification; Gherkin covers preserving responsibilities. MCP JSON-RPC tests verify the same policy at all twelve recipe boundaries.
records.missingDecision: Preserve EPIC -> FEAT -> Phase -> Task criteria and many-to-many test/criterion/code links. FEAT and Phase use applicable isolated tests; EPIC owns complete workflow E2E. Passing TwinTests do not replace assigned E2E obligations. Reproduce bugs at the right boundary and trace to missing focused coverage and code.

records.summary: Honor independent declared phase gates instead of role and file heuristics
records.whyHappened: Verification inferred mandatory checks from roles and source changes; the scanner contradicted justified N/A flags and invented browser obligations from UI files.
records.causalChain: Role/file classification overrode declared applicability -> data-only and documentation phases acquired hidden tests/reviews -> unnecessary completion blockers.
records.testGap: Existing tests enforced the unwanted file/role assumptions. Replace them with generic applicability cases and a runtime declaration-change matrix across roles, independent review and verification flags, configured integration execution, and an explicitly required browser negative case.
records.missingDecision: Use explicit independent gate declarations. Ordered tasks govern native requirements and developer revisions must synchronize contract and ledger. Required missing/failed checks and unresolved review findings stay blocked.

records.summary: Introduce versioned JSON exchange enforcement and phase-specific verification rules
records.whyHappened: Evidence projection reconstructed decisions from generated headings and test filenames. Repeated format fixes could either discard valid execution or become too permissive. A final-checkpoint role was also classified as production implementation without actual code changes.
records.causalChain: Unstructured handoffs and uniform assumptions about code-bearing phases -> ambiguous or misclassified verification -> repeated readiness blockers or unjustified exemptions
records.testGap: Generic schema tests cover mandatory and conditional fields, optional invalid audit metadata, duplicate decision keys, scope binding and representation-only recovery. Executable Gherkin scenarios run real Node assertions, build syntax checks and warning-emitting processes through the host executor, persist JSON and inspect phase readiness. Planning applicability, zero/failing tests, missing/corrupt JSON, configured-command mismatch and independent role changes are covered.
records.missingDecision: One versioned JSON schema package supplies sender contract and runtime validation. Migrate native phase verification and repair request/response as complete boundaries. Host outcomes, admitted roles and configured checks remain authoritative. Optional bookkeeping never certifies or invalidates execution. Documentation-only phases can declare N/A; checkpoints check health without requiring edits. Preserve explicit legacy import for unmigrated actions and do not claim universal migration.

records.summary: Recognise descriptive checkpoint suites and Rust test suffixes without erasing executed evidence
records.whyHappened: Checkpoint parsing required the literal word test in a suite label and filename classification recognised tests.rs but omitted prefixed Rust test modules. Passing suites with ignored counts and successful empty supporting targets could then be treated as failed or missing execution.
records.causalChain: Descriptive suite labels and Rust test suffixes -> existing execution and changed-test evidence discarded -> completed phase falsely blocked before continuation
records.testGap: Earlier fixtures used labels ending in tests and a narrow set of test filenames. New generic failing-first cases vary suite names, runner commands, Rust suffixes, aggregate ignored counts, empty targets and unresolved outcomes. Lifecycle integration runs real passing/failing Node assertions and checks next-phase dispatch without a changed-test filename fallback.
records.missingDecision: Identify checkpoint execution by semantic suite labels, commands or recorded counts; preserve literal command spelling. Aggregate ignored/skipped counts remain visible without being credited as passed or automatically treated as missing feature coverage. Explicit required-check gaps, failures, discovery and incomplete outcomes remain unresolved. Counted shorthand is recognised. Successful command-only summaries and explicitly empty supporting targets are neutral only alongside actual passing execution. This affects phase projection, not fresh readiness report validation.

records.summary: Recognise existing phase execution and review evidence across Markdown layouts and test languages
records.whyHappened: A review table's Decision header was interpreted as a verdict before the explicit APPROVED status. Wrapped changed-file inventories lost test files; test-name recognition omitted common non-JavaScript conventions. Checkpoint command/result tables were not projected as recorded test outcomes.
records.causalChain: Passing phase execution and approved review -> incomplete or incorrect evidence projection -> resolved phase reported missing tests and review -> continuation blocked before the next phase
records.testGap: Failing-first generic cases reproduce header shadowing, wrapped inventories, cross-language file names and checkpoint outcomes. Lifecycle Gherkin integration executes a real synthetic passing or failing subprocess, scans Markdown, persists workflow state in SQLite and asserts whether the next authorised phase is dispatched. Documentation-only applicability remains covered independently of phase number.
records.missingDecision: Evidence projection must use semantic fields rather than column labels, line wrapping or JavaScript naming assumptions. Preserve actual failed or unexecuted outcomes. Recorded checkpoint summaries serve phase continuation; they do not become verified native receipts or authorise feature completion.

records.summary: Accept equivalent console capture and exclude inherited planning prose from execution handoffs
records.whyHappened: A successful native test run added only console redirection to its recorded command, causing root receipt rejection. A separate live run showed setup instructions alone were insufficient: full check reasons were serialized into both the execution prompt and the receipt context, repeating unsupported historical dependency claims.
records.causalChain: Independent native report plus added audit capture -> string mismatch -> valid tests rejected; structurally wide checks -> historical reasons copied as execution context -> invented prerequisite repeated
records.testGap: Failing-first shared-import and HTTP cases reproduce console-only mismatch and inherited-reason leakage. Generic negatives cover altered selection, native outputs, outside/mismatched logs, append mode, shell expansions and statements. FV-20 executes a real subprocess writing native JSON separately from redirected console; FV-21 proves executable-field projection and minimal receipt context using a synthetic unrelated-service claim, preserving the full audit plan.
records.missingDecision: Separate execution identity and native evidence from optional presentation and planning explanations. Permit narrowly equivalent run-owned capture while retaining native validation and immutable receipts. Allowlist fields across execution handoff boundaries, rather than trusting a TypeScript structural type to remove extra runtime properties. Model interpretation of subsequently read source remains outside this deterministic projection guarantee.

records.summary: Ground setup in current configuration and preserve qualified native execution evidence
records.whyHappened: A generated planning report introduced an unsupported external service dependency. Later notes and cached plans repeated it, causing execution workers to skip configured browser checks. Separately, valid dirty-source qualification used hash-first wording rejected by the importer, and an aggregate wrapper emitted counts without native identities while hiding prebuilt execution.
records.causalChain: Unsupported planning claim -> repeated recovery prose -> cached prerequisite -> skipped execution; qualified hash-first revision -> formatting rejection; opaque wrapper -> summary-only evidence
records.testGap: Earlier tests did not exercise the hash-first source qualification or collections of more than two native reports. Failing-first shared importer tests now cover both, with negative ambiguous revisions, missing/duplicate/changed reports and conflicting bindings. FV-19 executes actual synthetic assertion processes through HTTP and browser confirmation. A separate HTTP regression injects an obsolete contract baseline with an unrelated service claim and verifies reinspection, replacement selection and fresh process execution. The inspection adapter is controlled; these tests do not prove arbitrary live-model dependency reasoning.
records.missingDecision: Use a shared current-source setup instruction contract across planning, correction and execution. Require exact dependency references and inspect wrapper delegation, while retaining bounded setup authority and native evidence. Contract hash changes invalidate old plans without rewriting project documents or old receipts. Accept equivalent qualified revision presentation and bounded multiple-native-report bindings without accepting aggregate prose or ambiguous source claims.

records.summary: Resolve configured nested Cargo manifests before executing and caching verification commands
records.whyHappened: Plan admission verified that a nested manifest existed but not whether the command could discover it from cwd. Execution workers corrected the missing manifest option after failure while the saved plan remained unchanged, causing repeated receipt-command rejection.
records.causalChain: Configured nested manifest -> missing command option -> failed lookup -> worker adds option -> successful retry differs from cached plan -> receipt rejection repeats
records.testGap: FV-18 fails before application wiring because the process-backed manifest resolver cannot find its configured workspace. Generic unit coverage verifies options, workspace discovery, explicit paths, ambiguity, literal shell quoting and baseline persistence. HTTP/browser flow executes the corrected preparation command and real synthetic tests, establishes readiness after human confirmation and reruns the saved correction on another Refresh. A separate HTTP test imports a legacy cached omission and verifies original/correction/context/receipt/baseline consistency.
records.missingDecision: Resolve an unambiguous missing manifest from current declared configuration before any execution. Validate and persist the corrected plan and preserve before/after audit records. Keep one command binding for context, execution, native import and reuse. Do not accept arbitrary worker command changes, use historical receipts as configuration authority, or require optional runId/timestamps.

records.summary: Do not block valid execution evidence on receipt timestamp recording errors
records.whyHappened: The optional-runId correction introduced a mandatory worker-authored timestamp gate. A worker recorded a future time after actual test execution, blocking all reports. Comparing with Date.now also changed the first diagnosis when identical evidence was inspected later.
records.causalChain: Valid execution reports -> inaccurate audit timestamp -> time-dependent receipt rejection -> feature completion blocked by bookkeeping
records.testGap: Failing-first shared importer cases cover absent, null, invalid, old and future timestamps with and without runId, unchanged artifact bytes and clock-independent revalidation. Negative cases retain missing/corrupt reports, failed execution and command/identity mismatches. FV-13 and FV-15 through FV-17 run actual synthetic assertion processes and reach readiness through HTTP and browser human confirmation while both timestamp metadata and runId remain uncorrected.
records.missingDecision: Receipt verifiedAt is optional audit metadata, never an independent admission gate. Remove its wall-clock comparison without inventing replacement timestamps. Preserve current-run output isolation, source guards, selected-check binding, native-report checks and human acceptance. Legacy conflicting-outcome ordering is unchanged. This supersedes the timestamp requirement in WJ-2026-101.

records.summary: Accept equivalent working-directory prefixes without changing executed test selection
records.whyHappened: Tests executed in the correct directory, but receipt commands included cd to that directory while inspected commands stored cwd separately. Exact string comparison rejected all evidence before native report validation.
records.causalChain: Correct cwd and test execution -> equivalent cwd prefix in receipt -> string inequality -> readiness blocked on formatting
records.testGap: Failing-first cases reproduce unquoted/quoted/escaped paths and cwd prefixes on shared import. Negatives preserve different directory, command/filter/manifest/report-path rejection. FV-14 invokes actual synthetic test processes through bash cd-prefix commands and retains that receipt representation through HTTP and browser readiness. Shared-import tests verify unchanged receipt bytes and identical phase/Refresh evidence identities.
records.missingDecision: Compare a narrowly defined equivalent presentation: a single literal cd to the configured cwd joined with && and an unchanged remaining command. Never execute text to normalize it or ignore actual selection/configuration changes. Keep one shared binding policy and native importer, preserving raw artifacts.

records.summary: Keep invocation IDs normally produced but optional for evidence admission
records.whyHappened: The importer made a model-written correlation field mandatory, and the producer fallback introduced another gate requiring a narrow shell event shape. Valid reports could fail solely because ID metadata was missing. The user clarified that runId should normally exist but its absence must not stop the process.
records.causalChain: Optional bookkeeping treated as execution proof -> omitted field or unavailable enrichment -> otherwise valid evidence blocked
records.testGap: Failing-first shared importer tests omit/null/empty the ID. A real-process HTTP test disables enrichment and expects evidence assessment to continue. FV-12 prevents optional archival enrichment and verifies the actual canonical receipt remains ID-less through browser readiness; FV-13 rejects yesterday's timestamp without an ID. Units also reject stale/future/invalid timestamps with IDs present, showing metadata cannot manufacture freshness.
records.missingDecision: HEPHA continues to supply IDs normally. Enrichment is best-effort and native import is authoritative whether or not an ID is present. Current verification uses existing verifiedAt, output directory and source guards; explicit conflicting identity claims remain invalid. Missing metadata alone never changes a valid result to failure. Use the current contract rather than old receipts as schema authority.

records.summary: Own invocation metadata in receipt production and test worker omissions through Refresh
records.whyHappened: The scoped importer required runId but the shared concrete JSON template omitted it. Tests populated runId themselves and verified rejection when absent, leaving the producer-to-importer handoff untested.
records.causalChain: Template omits runId -> worker follows template after executing tests -> importer correctly rejects unbound receipt -> fresh readiness blocks
records.testGap: Failing-first tests reproduce missing template and missing receipt metadata. FV-10 intentionally omits runId after real synthetic assertion subprocesses and verifies server-produced identity and untouched original evidence through both HTTP and browser flows. FV-11 rejects an explicitly wrong ID. Units reject unobserved, errored, printed or conditional commands, wrong bindings, symlinks and old receipts; corrupt/missing reports remain rejected by the same importer.
records.missingDecision: Invocation identity belongs to HEPHA. Persist context before execution, parameterize the shared JSON template, and finalize only current owned source-stable runs. Supply an absent ID only after exact selected-check binding and observed successful direct invocations for claimed passes. Preserve raw receipt; never rewrite explicit identity conflicts, command changes, outcomes or reports. One shared binding helper and one read-only evidence importer prevent divergent validators.

records.summary: Preserve documented verification scope across unchanged refreshes and correct original plan defects precisely
records.whyHappened: Identical instructions regenerated different paths. Rejected checks caused misleading phase errors; correction investigated unaffected mappings and retransmitted the plan until timeout. Activity tracking also consumed a newline delimiter.
records.causalChain: Reconstruct unchanged scope -> path drift -> cascading phase errors -> unnecessary investigation and full-plan output -> timeout before tests
records.testGap: Repeat-refresh tests asserted execution but allowed replanning. New failing-first tests cover persisted plan reuse, renamed documented tests, linked source/configuration/requirements changes, corrupt data and original diagnostics. Shared HTTP/SQLite and browser Twins execute real synthetic checks using the same inventory changes.
records.missingDecision: FeatureDescription.md is the test inventory entry point with explicit references to project/phase configuration. Maintain it with test changes. Revalidate a durable plan against identity, requirements, contract, phase mappings and source snapshots, rebind run destinations and always execute fresh checks. Correct diagnosed fields through small validated patches. Separate observed testing, supporting checks and waiting from evidence of success.

records.summary: Normalize the single verification-plan handoff before targeted correction and actual test dispatch
records.whyHappened: The parser rejected explanatory prose around otherwise semantically valid JSON. Correction used full inspection workers that repeated repository investigation and returned the same presentation wrapper, exhausting retries before test execution.
records.causalChain: Valid embedded plan -> presentation parse failure -> full correction investigation -> valid embedded plan rejected again -> correction exhaustion -> zero tests dispatched
records.testGap: Plan tests used plain JSON and did not prove that wrapped worker output reaches real test processes and the shared evidence importer. Correction tests covered cancellation and budget errors but not canonical candidates or shorter correction runtime propagation.
records.missingDecision: Decode one unambiguous payload deterministically, retain the existing semantic validation and persist its canonical plan. Do not use a model for harmless formatting. Unresolved typed errors receive at most two targeted corrections with three-minute runtime bounds; semantic candidates and precise diagnostics replace broad reinspection instructions. Keep raw output for audit, expose correction reason and elapsed time, and never bypass execution/evidence or human acceptance gates.

records.summary: Remove the parallel Refresh report validator and reuse the existing execution evidence importer
records.whyHappened: Refresh introduced independent receipt validation around the shared native parser. Supplemental bindings, revision validation, evidence IDs and non-test results diverged from phase/repair import. The Refresh prompt also combined conflicting output destinations and reuse instructions.
records.causalChain: Two receipt validators -> inconsistent evidence treatment -> maintenance drift and repeated blocked Refresh attempts
records.testGap: Separate happy-path fixtures could not prove shared implementation. Failing-first parameterized units now exercise the same scenarios for phase/repair/Refresh; the HTTP integration runs actual assertion subprocesses, spies on the real importer without stubbing it, and compares the same receipt's canonical evidence through both entry points.
records.missingDecision: One importer owns report interpretation and one prompt contract owns receipt production. Caller-specific run/check binding and current-source snapshots restrict which execution is eligible, not what passing evidence means. Silent successful non-test logs remain non-coverage; unsupported or failed tests stay blocked. No client-specific repair or human acceptance changes.

records.summary: Validate mixed verification plans and expose actual execution stages
records.whyHappened: Inspection returned automated tests alongside build, lint and discovery checks. A test-only validator rejected empty test paths on non-test checks before execution. Generic refresh and finalization labels concealed the blocked handoff.
records.causalChain: Mixed plan -> non-test check treated as test -> plan rejected -> zero executions -> no new evidence despite Refresh
records.testGap: The old Twin supplied an ideal test-only plan. Failing-first units now reproduce mixed classification, overlapping suite selection and single-error diagnostics. FV-08 corrects a synthetic mixed plan, runs real assertion subprocesses, and checks browser execution and assessment labels while those stages are held active.
records.missingDecision: Typed checks preserve legitimate non-test work without counting it as test coverage. Aggregate validation errors permit at most two scoped corrections, never retries for budget/runtime failure or cancellation. Server stages distinguish inspection, correction, preparation, planned test tool dispatch, report validation and evidence assessment; active verification is not finalization.

records.summary: Separate explicit cumulative spending policy from model context and preserve stopped inspection progress
records.whyHappened: A productive multi-turn inspection fit the selected model context but repeated history exhausted a hidden cumulative input ceiling before tests could start. Re-settling an already terminal single-route invocation hid the policy stop behind a persistence failure, and raw usage telemetry flooded the feature card.
records.causalChain: Growing inspection history -> implicit cumulative cap -> worker exit before complete plan -> duplicate terminal settlement -> misleading error and no test evidence
records.testGap: Prior synthetic workers skipped the multi-request runtime guard. Failing-first unit tests reproduced the hidden cap and one-route persistence misclassification; FV-07 runs the same budget-stop/checkpoint/retry journey through browser and server Twin. Real subprocess tests invoke the request guard repeatedly with and without an explicit cap.
records.missingDecision: Model context remains mandatory; cumulative local input spending becomes an explicit optional operator limit. A configured cap stops before dispatch without fallback or automatic retry. Preserve bounded partial inspection navigation and revalidate it on a later explicit Refresh, never as coverage or execution evidence. Keep telemetry in logs and show a concise policy error. Changed or malformed checkpoint data is not reused.

records.summary: Make explicit Refresh verify current feature source before assessing coverage
records.whyHappened: The old coordinator trusted historical passes and required an execution-gap classification before dispatch. Investigation gaps stopped without inspecting repository setup, and later code changes could leave obsolete reports as apparent proof.
records.causalChain: Historical pass or investigation classification -> no verification worker -> no fresh reports -> readiness repeatedly assessed old evidence
records.testGap: Failing-first admission tests returned historical ready status with zero workers. Browser journeys also reproduced an enabled Refresh button during active verification. New shared Gherkin/browser/server twins execute synthetic assertion processes across phase scopes and prove failure, skip, missing-report, source-drift, repeat-refresh and cancellation behavior.
records.missingDecision: Explicit Refresh owns bounded inspection of all feature phases, deduplicated configured test execution, current source-content snapshots, run-local native reports and subsequent coverage assessment. Historical automated evidence cannot fill a current-run hole. Manual outcomes and approval history remain stored; acceptance and completion stay human-owned. Background assessment never executes tests. Verification failures require explicit repair rather than weakened tests or silent correction.

records.summary: Apply pinned token budgeting and lossless reference grouping to verification action routing
records.whyHappened: Coverage assessment received model capacity but action routing retained a fixed character guard. Repeated partial-reference explanations inflated the next prompt and prevented the execution handoff despite sufficient model token capacity. An optional empty test-path array also caused a full assessment correction.
records.causalChain: Coverage accepted -> accumulated partial context plus phase source -> legacy routing character guard -> no target selection or verification worker
records.testGap: Failing-first generic unit tests reproduced rejection of a large character payload that fit model token capacity, including correction, and 151 repeated reference entries instead of one grouped projection. CR-15 now exercises large routing context through real application/HTTP/SQLite, synthetic worker reports, automatic reassessment and separate human confirmation in both browser and server-only runners.
records.missingDecision: Every production routing request uses the pinned model counter/capacity, correction headroom and shared spending guard. Apply progressive lossless compaction, complete-criterion partitioning and existing validated source retrieval without inventing coverage or deleting qualifications. Group repeated references but retain distinct assertions and unchanged durable approvals. Stop before futile source extraction when non-source context alone cannot fit.

records.summary: Close the discovered-test to execution-evidence handoff in supervised Refresh and repair
records.whyHappened: Refresh only assessed evidence and never dispatched identified unrun verification. A returned repair worker was recorded completed even when it merely created tests and its selected gate remained unresolved.
records.causalChain: Discovered test -> missing run report -> assessment-only refresh -> no producer of execution evidence; worker return -> completed attempt despite unresolved selected verification
records.testGap: Failing-first integration reproduced zero worker calls from a user refresh with configured unrun tests. A second regression reproduced completed repair status after a created-tests claim with no executed report. CR-13/CR-14 share browser and server-twin scenarios, alongside CR-09 blocked prerequisites.
records.missingDecision: Explicit user Refresh may dispatch one current configured verification phase with actual preflight. The worker must execute after repair, save source-bound native reports/receipts, diagnose actual failures and attempt only bounded in-scope correction. Missing prerequisites remain blocked. Background settlement invokes assessment only, never another worker. No configuration guesses, duplicate tests, fabricated evidence or automatic human acceptance.

records.summary: Consolidate supervised refresh and unresolved reassessment into one server-decided action
records.whyHappened: Two buttons exposed an internal cache decision to the user, who explicitly requested a single Refresh action that decides when reassessment is necessary.
records.causalChain: Cached refresh and fresh-decision authority exposed separately -> repeated no-op user clicks and unnecessary operational choice

records.summary: Bind recovery actions to configured verification targets and preserve prerequisite gates across reassessment

records.missingDecision: Discover a bounded static project target catalog without evaluating configuration. records.summary: Fit interleaved execution catalogues losslessly within the correction-aware assessment budget

Prompt-keyed checkpoints invalidate changed encodings while retaining unchanged extraction stages; coverage truth and human authority do not change.

records.summary: Recover malformed assessor envelopes with bounded correction and value-free field diagnostics

records.summary: Distinguish identified tests from executed coverage and route missing execution through explicit prerequisites

records.summary: Preserve compatibility phase gate applicability and recognise nested review evidence

This projection does not rerun verification, grant waivers, or establish current-HEAD review coverage.

records.summary: Expose actionable phase quality blockers and enforce them before compatibility advancement
records.whyHappened: Compatibility execution validated artifact structure and completion statuses but not phase quality projections. Dashboard recovery then hid a real validation failure when all phase checkboxes were completed, and completion showed only an aggregate gap count.
records.causalChain: worker marks phase complete -> structural validator passes -> next phase dispatched despite missing quality evidence -> final artifact failure hidden by completed-phase projection -> completion panel reports aggregate gaps without resolution instructions
records.testGap: No scanner-backed integration required missing phase evidence to block the next dispatch or finalization, and browser tests did not inspect each gap or preserve a malformed-artifact error after phases completed.
records.missingDecision: Quality evidence is independently required at phase boundaries. Missing or unrecognised evidence is not an executed failure. Show each phase/gate, recorded diagnostics and references, inspect controls and conditional resolution guidance; do not silently clear evidence or alter release policy.

records.summary: Recover partial implementation transitions under deterministic evidence checks
records.whyHappened: A start worker moved the feature folder but left its task header Ready. Continue rejected the artifact before a repair could run, despite existing completed phases.
records.causalChain: Non-atomic agent file updates -> inconsistent lifecycle projections -> validation failure -> hidden Continue action -> unrelated preparation controls remained visible.
records.testGap: No end-to-end fixture exercised a stale Ready header after a successful start, a claimed but missing move, or a recovery worker that invented progress.
records.missingDecision: Recovery eligibility is distinct from valid artifacts. Admit only known partial transitions, repair within the same workflow, verify unique filesystem location and preserved evidence, and keep real gates or uncertain state blocked. Recovery has one attempt and a two-minute worker deadline; model output cannot declare recovery success.

records.summary: Render normal preparation actions independently from recovery diagnostics
records.whyHappened: Design was rendered only through missing-design recovery reasons, while submitted readiness intentionally evaluates unresolved markers rather than implementation prerequisites.
records.causalChain: Deep-Dive completed -> backend authorized design -> submitted readiness had no recovery reasons -> UI displayed neither Design nor blocked Refine.
records.testGap: Existing browser coverage supplied a missing-design reason and never exercised a submitted feature with authorized Design and empty recovery reasons.
records.missingDecision: Backend action availability, not diagnostic messages, must control normal preparation buttons.

records.summary: Allow voluntary focused feature interviews and preserve preparation gates across recipe providers
records.whyHappened: Deep-Dive actions were exposed only for recovery markers; classification attempts were deduplicated by card identity and compatibility refinement bypassed design prerequisites.
records.causalChain: A clarified feature changed -> classification became unknown but was not retried -> the compatibility Refine action remained enabled -> no voluntary interview control allowed the human to steer additional exploration.
records.testGap: Tests covered mandatory recovery but not repeated marker-free interviews with persisted focus, conflicting active runs, or revision-sensitive classification retries.
records.missingDecision: Human-requested exploration is independent of required recovery, and recipe providers cannot authorize skipping preparation prerequisites.

records.summary: Establish one diagnostic workflow map and causal change gate
records.whyHappened: Workflow behavior was documented across command YAML, lifecycle prose, focused architecture notes, production applications, and tests, so an operator could observe a wrong transition without one diagram that identified its owner.
records.causalChain: Incremental workflow changes added correct local documentation and tests -> no repository-wide transition registry connected those fragments -> incident diagnosis required broad code and log searches -> the exact decision boundary was slow to identify.
records.testGap: No test asserted that every documented transition had a real production Class.method owner, unit evidence, Gherkin evidence, and a matching Mermaid edge, or that every declared YAML command node remained represented in the architecture map.
records.missingDecision: The architecture had no explicit decision that one registry and map are the diagnostic authority, and no mandatory causal justification record for future workflow changes.

records.summary: Route unresolved refinement decisions back to interactive Deep-Dive
records.whyHappened: A refinement worker correctly stopped after discovering an unresolved architecture decision, but its plain-text blocker exited successfully. The generic worker labelled the process completed, RefineFeature unconditionally entered promotion, and the missing-artifact validator became the first component able to reject the run.
records.causalChain: Deep-Dive inspected only the current source and validation markers -> refinement later inspected dependency contracts and found a contradiction -> the result contract had no machine-readable blocker branch -> RefineFeature ignored response semantics and ran artifact validation -> the catch boundary recorded failed instead of blocked.
records.testGap: Unit and Gherkin coverage modelled only valid artifacts, invalid artifacts, and recovery from already-valid durable artifacts. No scenario supplied a successful worker process with unresolved user questions, asserted that artifact validation was skipped, created an interactive question session, or repeated Deep-Dive and refinement without a round limit.
records.missingDecision: The workflow lacked the invariant that unresolved user-owned planning decisions are a durable NEEDS_DEEP_DIVE outcome, not an operational failure, and lacked a transition from refinement evaluation to the existing answer/chat session contract.

records.summary: Separate historical phase-contract readability from current refinement authoring
records.whyHappened: The canonical Refine Feature command required PhaseExecutionContract V3, but the installed Pi Refine skill still requested V2. The artifact validator used the same permissive parser needed for historical execution and therefore allowed the stale worker output to authorize readiness.
records.causalChain: Two Refine Feature instruction sources diverged -> the invoked Pi skill emitted V2 -> the compatibility parser correctly read V2 -> refinement promotion reused that reader without a current-authoring policy -> a new feature reached Ready without the mandatory V3 phase Git checkpoints.
records.testGap: Contract parser tests proved V2 compatibility and V3 checkpoint structure separately, but no unit or Gherkin scenario asserted that new refinement promotion rejects V1/V2 while historical implementation continues to read them. No parity test compared the command template and installed Pi skill contract version.
records.missingDecision: The architecture had not explicitly separated read compatibility from authoring authority at the Refine Feature promotion boundary, and had no invariant requiring all live Refine instruction sources to name the current contract version.

records.summary: Resume provider-refused workers through one fresh Continue Implementing session
records.whyHappened: A worker's generated tool-call history became corrupted and the model provider rejected the next accumulated prompt. The active implementation task had durable progress, but Hepha classified the provider refusal as non-recoverable and failed the phase instead of discarding only the contaminated session.
records.causalChain: Provider rejected the accumulated worker request -> ImplementationWorkerApplication preserved the provider error -> ImplementationAutoRecoveryApplication consulted the recoverable whitelist before selecting a retry route -> the classifier had no provider-prompt-refusal category -> the run entered terminal phase failure although the durable task was resumable.
records.testGap: Classifier tests did not include provider prompt refusal, automatic-recovery tests mocked every candidate as recoverable and did not assert the Continue Implementing command, worker tests did not prove that successive worker identities receive different session files, and no Gherkin scenario required same-task fresh-session recovery with a one-attempt bound.
records.missingDecision: The workflow lacked the invariant that conversational session state is disposable while phase/task/review state is durable, and lacked an explicit transition from provider input refusal to Continue Implementing at the same unfinished task.

records.summary: Preserve Continue eligibility through authoritative V3 inventory selection
records.whyHappened: The generic phase-template validator still required a legacy Phase and Status table even when PhaseExecutionContract V3 was authoritative. Its alignment circuit inserted that compatibility table before the V3 inventory, while the execution artifact validator parsed only the first table in the section.
records.causalChain: V3 refinement produced a valid contract inventory -> legacy dispatch validation rejected the absence of a Phase column -> alignment added a legacy table -> execution validation selected the first table positionally -> CONTRACT_INVENTORY_MISMATCH set hasRefinementArtifacts=false -> readiness suppressed Continue after an unrelated provider refusal.
records.testGap: Phase-template unit tests covered only the legacy Phase and Status inventory, artifact-contract tests covered only a single table in the Phase Inventory section, and no Gherkin scenario proved that a current contract inventory remains authoritative when a historical projection is also present.
records.missingDecision: The architecture had not stated that versioned inventory schema outranks Markdown table position, nor that failed-run action eligibility must be recomputed from that authoritative durable contract instead of the presentation order of compatibility projections.

records.summary: Unify phase-status reconciliation behind the contract inventory projection
records.whyHappened: Readiness and template validation had been migrated to the V3 Contract ID, Document, Role, and Status inventory, but reconciliation, phase scanning, phase entry, completion, and recovery snapshots retained independent numeric Phase table parsers and writers.
records.causalChain: Continue became correctly eligible -> current FeatureTasks contained only its canonical V3 inventory -> pre-run reconciliation searched for a row beginning with the numeric phase -> it returned no FeatureTasks status -> the fail-closed reconciliation policy rejected Phase 2 before any worker dispatch.
records.testGap: Every reconciliation and status-persistence fixture used the legacy numeric Phase table, while V3 contract tests ended at artifact validation. No unit or Gherkin integration test carried a V3 inventory through the production reconciliation read, promotion write, phase-entry write, scanner read, and recovery snapshot path.
records.missingDecision: The architecture defined the V3 contract as authoring authority but did not require all FeatureTasks lifecycle consumers to share one schema-selected status projection with a legacy fallback only when no contract inventory exists.

records.summary: Make contracted design documents part of Deep-Dive freshness
records.whyHappened: HEPHA recorded and compared Deep-Dive freshness using only FeatureDescription.md. Design Feature was introduced later and created authoritative satellite reports, but the freshness boundary and Deep-Dive prompt remained single-document contracts.
records.causalChain: An initial FEAT Deep-Dive recorded the Feature Description hash -> Design Feature created UX, wireframe, and summary documents containing assumptions and unresolved decisions -> the scanner hashed only the unchanged Feature Description -> HEPHA classified Deep-Dive as current and exposed refinement -> refinement became the first workflow able to discover the unresolved cross-document decisions.
records.testGap: Deep-Dive tests proved that changes to one source string become stale, while Design Feature tests proved only that three artifacts exist. No unit or Gherkin scenario joined the two workflows by creating design output after a completed Deep-Dive, asserting that refinement becomes unavailable, supplying every design document to the next question round, and recording the combined completion hash.
records.missingDecision: The architecture had not classified contracted design artifacts as authoritative preparation inputs and had no deterministic document-set identity shared by scanner freshness, question planning, completion evidence, and continuation recovery.

records.summary: Enforce changed-code test coverage at declared final checkpoints
records.whyHappened: The final verification runner proved configured commands returned green but had no coverage intent, no machine-report schema, and no relationship between implementation work and the tests that executed it. RefineFeature therefore could not declare or validate a measurable coverage obligation.
records.causalChain: RefineFeature emitted a full-verification task -> the project profile ran build, typecheck, and unit tests -> green command exits completed the task -> untested changed production lines could reach phase completion because no baseline-aware LCOV decision existed.
records.testGap: Final-verification tests covered profile syntax, required build/test/lint intents, command outcomes, warning detection, and repair loops, but no unit test parsed changed Git lines or LCOV evidence and no generic Gherkin scenario kept a final checkpoint active below a coverage floor.
records.missingDecision: The workflow had not decided that a declared final checkpoint must connect RefineFeature's declarative test-coverage requirement to the durable StartFeature commit and a project-owned machine-readable report. RefineFeature must reuse a valid project profile across FEATs. A project with no configured coverage asks once through Deep-Dive for the command, LCOV report path, source selectors, and multi-stack ownership, then persists that answer in the project profile rather than guessing, failing, or asking every FEAT. Workflows that deliberately declare no final checkpoint remain unmodified.

records.summary: Make test-coverage thresholds advisory and visible at FEAT scope
records.whyHappened: The first coverage circuit correctly measured code introduced since StartFeature, but classified a percentage below 80 as a failed required check. That confused a quality-improvement signal with a red test or broken coverage command and could keep an otherwise valid phase in an unlimited repair loop.
records.causalChain: Coverage command and tests exited green -> LCOV successfully measured FEAT changed lines -> one measured file was below 80 percent -> the adapter changed the required check to failed -> the generic verifier repeatedly dispatched repair -> phase completion depended on a percentage even though the engineering policy intended a reminder and aspirational target.
records.testGap: Unit tests asserted that below-reference coverage failed, and Gherkin asserted that it remained unresolved without a retry cap. No acceptance scenario required phase/FEAT completion with a reminder, bounded project-configured improvement attempts, FEAT-only repair scope, separate overall project context, or a details-page assessment.
records.missingDecision: The architecture had not separated three concerns: command/test health is blocking, FEAT changed-line percentage is actionable but advisory, and overall project coverage is contextual only. It also lacked a declared limit and stop result for optional coverage improvement work, a durable UI projection for the latest receipt, and an explicit rule that staged, unstaged, and new production files before the phase git checkpoint belong to the FEAT baseline comparison.

records.summary: Require deterministic registered-action routing before a worker-dispatch boundary
records.whyHappened: Routing authority was distributed across static model options, environment defaults, and workflow fields, so a future worker could receive a model selection that was neither policy-revisioned nor validated against the current catalog.
records.causalChain: Static route inputs were read directly by command composition -> labels and environment values could select a route outside the durable policy -> unavailable or incapable catalog facts were not uniformly rejected -> a later execution boundary could receive an accidental model choice.
records.testGap: No public resolver test proved atomic first-route bootstrap, Action to Action Type to Global precedence, exact identity preservation, and rejection-before-plan for unavailable or incapable routes. No backend Gherkin contract described the no-execution result boundary.
records.missingDecision: The workflow lacked the invariant that every worker-producing action first resolves through one registered V1 action and persisted policy, returning only a typed plan or sanitized rejection; no resolver may spawn, inject credentials, write receipts, or advance workflow state.

records.summary: Resolve a concurrent bootstrap contender through the persisted Global winner
records.whyHappened: The bootstrap mutation was transaction-safe, but the resolver projected a transaction conflict directly even when another valid caller had already persisted the only Global revision.
records.causalChain: Two valid callers observed an unset policy -> one transaction persisted the Global revision -> the other mutation returned a conflict -> the resolver returned that conflict instead of rereading the durable winner -> a safe deterministic plan was unnecessarily withheld.
records.testGap: Resolver tests covered a successful bootstrap and ordinary rejection paths but did not stage a mutation conflict followed by a valid winning policy, no policy, an unreadable reread, or a registry-version mismatch. The backend Gherkin contract did not require conflict resolution without a second mutation.
records.missingDecision: The routing transition lacked the invariant that a bootstrap conflict is resolved by exactly one reread of the persisted current policy, accepting only the active registry version and never retrying mutation, substituting the contender route, or crossing the execution boundary.

records.summary: Treat unavailable test-coverage measurement as non-blocking telemetry
records.whyHappened: Coverage execution and measurement errors were represented with the same failed or policy-blocked outcomes used by authoritative build, lint/typecheck, and test checks. The generic verification executor therefore treated unavailable coverage evidence as permission to repair or stop the lifecycle even though coverage was introduced as developer decision-support telemetry.
records.causalChain: The coverage command failed or the StartFeature baseline, LCOV report, or instrumentation record was unavailable -> the adapter emitted a blocking outcome -> the generic verification application dispatched repair -> recovery could require an orchestrator restart or exhaust its repair route -> an otherwise green phase or FEAT failed because optional quality telemetry could not be measured.
records.testGap: Tests covered successful measurements, measured below-reference advisory results, and ordinary required-check failures, but no unit or Gherkin scenario required every coverage execution and measurement error to produce an exact visible remark, skip the improvement worker, preserve independent gates, and permit ordinary phase and FEAT completion.
records.missingDecision: The workflow had not explicitly separated three outcomes: independent build, lint/typecheck, and test failures are lifecycle gates; successfully measured below-reference FEAT coverage may enter a bounded improvement loop; and unavailable coverage measurement is a non-gating remark that must never fail or block the phase or FEAT.

records.summary: Connect the first Web workflow action to Pi's validated installation default
records.whyHappened: The policy resolver implemented atomic bootstrap when a caller supplied a route, but the generic Web workflow adapter always supplied null. At the same time the Pi catalog scanner parsed its supported command output as JSON even though the installed Pi returns a table, so the required safe catalog fact could not exist.
records.causalChain: Global policy was unset -> Continue Implementing entered the generic route adapter -> the adapter called policy resolution with bootstrap null -> the resolver correctly returned ROUTING_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIRED before launching Pi -> restart repeated the identical call. Independently, Pi catalog discovery ran pi --list-models -> JSON parsing rejected valid table output -> the catalog stayed empty -> even a future supplied installation route would have failed availability validation.
records.testGap: Resolver tests called RoutingPolicyService directly with a handcrafted bootstrap route and therefore bypassed the production RoutingActionResolver and startup catalog composition. Scanner tests used JSON fixtures rather than Pi's real supported table format. No unit or Gherkin scenario started with an empty policy and exercised the generic Web resolver through installation settings, connection identity, catalog validation, persisted Global creation, and runtime provider projection.
records.missingDecision: The routing map described a valid supplied bootstrap context but did not assign ownership for obtaining it. The missing invariant is that the generic Web adapter may retry only ROUTING_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIRED with Pi's explicit provider/model bound to exactly one active code-owned endpoint and exact available catalog identity; all other policy errors remain authoritative and no labels, workflow fields, environment aliases, or static fallbacks may supply a route.

records.summary: Replace model-key Pi runners with one guarded plan-bound isolated execution host
records.whyHappened: Routing ended at a typed HandoffPlanV1, while one-shot, detached, dashboard-task, and workflow worker runners projected the selected model into a temporary model-ID-keyed map and could fall back through a default key. That projection lost immutable connection identity, authentication version, and normalized runtime evidence at the process boundary.
records.causalChain: FEAT-061 resolved a complete accepted plan -> bootstrap composition reduced it to model strings for legacy runner signatures -> runners looked up a model map/default and inherited broad process environment -> launch-time route/authentication pinning and authoritative receipts were not guaranteed -> duplicate model IDs, credential isolation, and next-worker-only routing could not be proven through the real host path.
records.testGap: Existing runner tests exercised model-string lookup, process output, and detached lifecycle independently. No generic unit and backend Gherkin route passed an accepted plan through guard order, exact connection/authentication binding, launch-scoped vault transport, unique parallel contexts, normalized receipt writes, detached-exit cleanup, and deterministic no-substitute rejection.
records.missingDecision: The workflow lacked the invariant that every Pi launch API requires the complete accepted HandoffPlanV1 and that only HandoffPlanExecutor.executeAttempt may cross from plan to process. Model maps, default keys, optional plans, context-free launches, inherited credentials, and policy re-resolution at execution are forbidden.

records.summary: Keep stopped implementation manually continuable from execution authority
records.whyHappened: The dashboard reused complete refinement-artifact validation to authorize continuation. An implementation run stopped after a verification-receipt persistence error, and a malformed refinement-only architecture-debt satellite made hasRefinementArtifacts false even though the execution contract, unresolved phase cursor, and task ledger remained usable. The same persistence path also applied the 256-character identifier limit to schema-valid 4096-character verification evidence.
records.causalChain: The worker produced valid explanatory receipt evidence longer than an identifier -> the immutable-store projection rejected it as persistence_failed -> automatic recovery stopped and persisted a durable failure brief -> the workflow summary revalidated every refinement satellite -> one unrelated invalid satellite suppressed canContinueImplementing -> the Web client correctly rendered no button from the incorrect backend decision -> the operator had no manual recovery route.
records.testGap: Tests proved refinement promotion completeness and ordinary continuation from wholly valid artifacts, but no unit or Gherkin matrix covered failed, blocked, and cancelled runs with a valid execution contract plus an invalid refinement-only satellite. No UI test required the manual button in that state, and no storage-boundary test exercised verification evidence between 257 and 4096 characters.
records.missingDecision: The workflow did not explicitly separate refinement promotion authority from implementation continuation authority. WF-RECOVERY-STOP also lacked the explicit invariant that it ends only automatic recovery and cannot remove WF-CONTINUE-ELIGIBLE. Free-text evidence and identifiers shared a default bound despite different schema contracts.

records.summary: Recover an approved but nonterminal review on its unresolved declared task
records.whyHappened: A reviewer persisted a schema-valid APPROVED manifest, but the authoritative gate correctly remained PENDING / terminal_remediation_required because the preceding remediation response had no bound verification receipt. The dispatcher did not complete the declared review task, then still called phase exit, which converted the expected unresolved-task state into REVIEW_CONTRACT_V1_GATE_DENIED and stopped the workflow.
records.causalChain: A fixer response persisted without its verification receipt -> resume routing treated either a response or receipt as sufficient to invoke the reviewer -> the reviewer returned APPROVED -> publication selected phase_exit from the manifest result alone while authoritative ingestion returned PENDING -> dispatch correctly left the review task unchecked but fell through to phase exit -> the exit guard correctly rejected the unresolved task -> the outer workflow incorrectly recorded a terminal phase failure instead of recovering the same task.
records.testGap: Unit tests covered APPROVED-to-phase-exit and PENDING-gate rejection separately, while dispatch tests mocked every APPROVED publication as gateApproved. The Gherkin review-dispatch scenarios had no case combining an APPROVED manifest, PENDING / terminal_remediation_required gate, unchecked declared review task, and a later verification task. No restart scenario distinguished a response without a receipt from a complete response/receipt pair.
records.missingDecision: The workflow lacked the invariant that a review manifest result never completes a declared review task independently of its exact-scope authoritative gate. It also conflated a remediation response with the verification receipt required to hand control back to the reviewer. Nonterminal remediation must reselect the same review task and recover its evidence; only terminal authoritative approval may complete that task and expose the next declared task or phase exit.

records.summary: Classify one plan-authorized runtime hop from durable work evidence and preserve independent child lineage
records.whyHappened: The accepted routing provider could describe one optional second route and the isolated executor could run one primary, but no runtime owner classified that second route from durable substantive-work state. The first Phase 4 implementation then added direct and nested adapter classes without production callers, allowed a running source with work state none, wrote the handoff edge only after child completion, and classified persistence-authority failures as if they were safe route failures. The first remediation returned callable knowledge/direct methods and invoked them from tests, but index consumed only Code Review, so four methods remained outside real command and lifecycle paths.
records.causalChain: A primary route failed -> legacy workflow recovery interpreted free-form failure/output and launched another worker -> the first coordinator classified every failed executor result -> a persistence failure or work-state read rejection could reach step 1 -> standalone dispatch and bootstrap tests called adapters and returned methods that production phase/feature/completion/direct paths never consumed -> direct mismatch awaited child completion before recording the edge and could leave the source process live.
records.testGap: The plan provider tests stopped before execution, and initial Phase 4 tests called standalone adapters or returned bootstrap methods rather than DirectImplementationSkillApplication, PhaseReviewExecutionApplication, RuntimeKnowledgeWorkerLifecycleApplication, and detached completion. They lacked a process barrier, late-source and persistence matrices, route-match positive control, index caller audit, post-completion curator barrier, and production lifecycle coverage for all four nested actions.
records.missingDecision: The missing invariant was one chain-level authority plus explicit production entry ownership: RuntimeExecutionCoordinator may classify only terminal non-persistence primary failures; DirectSessionHandoffAdapter runs from the production direct command while the source is preparing and persists its edge before child work; every nested lifecycle method must be consumed in index and reached from review, phase exit, feature lessons, or successful detached completion, not merely returned or test-invoked.

records.summary: Start resumed specialist work without fabricating parent invocation lineage
records.whyHappened: The nested-specialist migration assumed every Code Review and knowledge action runs after a root model invocation in the same workflow run. Continue Implementing can instead create a new run and resume directly at an unresolved review task, so no current-run parent exists and the specialist failed before process launch with RUNTIME_PARENT_INVOCATION_REQUIRED.
records.causalChain: A prior implementation run left durable work awaiting review -> Continue created a fresh workflow run and selected the review task -> the production review boundary required nested execution -> findRuntimeParent searched only the new run -> no root invocation existed -> the worker failed before Pi launch and every retry repeated the same topology.
records.testGap: The production-composition test manually launched a synthetic parent prompt before every nested specialist. No unit or Gherkin scenario entered a specialist as the first model invocation of a resumed run, asserted current card/phase/task scope on its receipt, or prohibited a fake parent receipt.
records.missingDecision: The runtime contract defined nested lineage but did not define invocation topology when a durable workflow resumes directly at a specialist in a new run. The missing invariant is that nesting requires a real parent; the first actual model invocation in a resumed run is an independently planned, fully scoped root specialist chain.

records.summary: Replace the Refine Feature completion estimate with progress-based liveness and durable artifact resume
records.whyHappened: Refine Feature originally received a dedicated 15-minute total timeout when refinement was described as one large JSON response. The workflow evolved into a tool-enabled process that writes core planning artifacts and a refinement-defined number of phase files, but the estimated completion duration remained a process-killing safety boundary. A productive worker was terminated while writing phase artifacts, its runtime receipt still said workState none, and route-sequence exhaustion replaced the known timeout in the dashboard.
records.causalChain: A repository example value became the source fallback -> the worker inherited both implementation idle handling and the fixed Refine total timer -> valid writes continued near the deadline -> the wall-clock timer killed the process regardless of recent activity -> write/edit events were not connected to runtime mutation state -> the one-step coordinator returned RUNTIME_ROUTE_SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED -> the generic failure brief recommended implementation phase-task recovery instead of refinement artifact resume.
records.testGap: The old test asserted only that Refine Feature passed a dedicated timeout value to the worker. No fake-clock/process test proved that productive activity beyond that duration survives, no generic Gherkin route covered stall versus explicit maximum, no test projected arbitrary contract phase counts, and no runtime integration test asserted that a successful artifact write changes workState before a later stop.
records.missingDecision: The missing invariant was that refinement completion time is not a safety contract. Hepha must stop silent work through a resettable stall circuit, apply a wall-clock maximum only when explicitly configured, persist contract-derived artifact progress, move runtime state away from none before mutation, and resume a later run from durable files without automatic clean-start fallback.

records.summary: Recover valid Ready refinement after result-envelope drift and canonicalize architecture-debt query selectors
records.whyHappened: A resumed refinement correctly preserved four existing phases, created the four missing phases, validated the complete V3 handoff, and moved the FEAT to Ready, but returned repository-relative files entries instead of feature-relative Result V1 paths. Recovery then failed because a valid touch plan orders symbol records by relative path while the strict architecture-debt store requires the extracted symbol-name array itself to be lexically sorted; the adapter passed those independent query facts unsorted and translated invalid_input to store_unavailable.
records.causalChain: The prompt said durable artifact paths but did not repeat the schema's feature-relative boundary -> the worker included MemoryBank/lifecycle/FEAT prefixes -> the strict result parser rejected the envelope after filesystem success -> recovered completion evaluated architecture debt -> relative-path-ordered plan symbols produced a non-lexical symbol-name list -> the store rejected its query input -> recovery returned false and the dashboard recorded a failed Refine workflow despite valid Ready artifacts.
records.testGap: Parser tests covered unsupported paths and readiness tests covered sorted single-symbol fixtures separately. No execution test supplied an invalid COMPLETED envelope after Ready artifacts existed, and no architecture-debt integration fixture used symbols whose required relative-path order differed from symbol-name lexical order. Progress tests also did not distinguish creation of a missing phase from repair of an existing phase.
records.missingDecision: The missing invariant was that independent strict-boundary query selectors must be canonicalized at the adapter even when their source artifact has another valid ordering contract. Result V1 paths remain feature-relative, while a reporting failure after complete Ready artifacts must enter the existing fail-closed recovery gates rather than invalidate filesystem work. Existing artifact edits must be presented as repairs, not generation.

records.summary: Admit zero-based first phases at the plan-bound runtime context boundary
records.whyHappened: The V3 phase execution contract correctly declares phases with zero-based order, but the strict runtime attempt-context validator reused a positive-integer rule for phaseNumber.
