Start Implementing completed post-processing, selected Phase 0 and its first task, then rejected the invocation context before opening a runtime receipt or launching Pi.
records.causalChain: Refinement authored the required order-0 entry phase -> Start Implementing moved the FEAT to In Progress and selected its first unresolved task -> ImplementationWorkerApplication preserved phaseNumber 0 -> the plan-bound runner projected the exact context -> isRuntimeAttemptContextV1 required phaseNumber greater than zero -> RuntimeExecutionCoordinator returned RUNTIME_INVALID_CONTEXT -> the dashboard incorrectly described a host schema mismatch as an Implementation Agent failure.
records.testGap: Runtime executor and implementation-worker tests used only phases 2-4 even though generic phase contracts and production FEATs start at zero. No Gherkin runtime-boundary scenario asserted that a zero-based first phase reaches process launch, and failure-brief tests did not distinguish pre-launch host context rejection from worker failure.
records.missingDecision: The missing invariant was that phase order is a non-negative zero-based index, not a positive business identifier. Strict runtime validation must accept zero while still rejecting negative, fractional, malformed, or unpaired contract/phase context, and pre-launch rejection must be diagnosed as host runtime failure.

records.summary: Route exhausted phase tasks through mandatory exit and scope task authority to the declared ledger
records.whyHappened: Two independent shortcuts disagreed with the declared phase contract. First, a phase continuation result named phase_completed caused the autonomous loop to advance before PhaseExitLifecycleApplication, so FEAT-069 completed phases without their declared git checkpoints. After that shortcut was removed, FEAT-070 reached phase exit, where hasCheckedTaskLedger counted every Markdown checkbox in the document; unchecked machine sign-offs under Phase Checkpoint were misclassified as unresolved executable tasks even though both explicit Phase Task Ledger items and durable task rows were completed.
records.causalChain: The final declared task settled -> deterministic reconciliation projected the phase document as COMPLETED -> pre-review continuation returned phase_completed -> the old coordinator shortcut skipped phase exit and checkpoint; after routing was corrected -> phase exit refreshed the completed document -> the completion authorization scanned all document checkboxes -> independent checkpoint sign-offs remained unchecked -> authorization threw an unresolved-task failure -> Continue Implementation retried the same contradictory boundary because the contract queue correctly had no task to dispatch.
records.testGap: Coordinator tests exercised review-ready exit but not an advance_phase continuation with a declared checkpoint. Status-repository fixtures contained task checkboxes only, and task-ledger tests had no explicit Phase Task Ledger followed by an independent unchecked checkpoint checklist. No Gherkin scenario asserted that non-ledger checkboxes cannot become executable work, and the generic failure brief blamed a worker instead of the host authority disagreement.
records.missingDecision: The missing invariant was that deterministic task settlement may update durable phase presentation but never bypasses the mandatory phase-exit boundary. When an explicit Phase Task Ledger exists, it is the only Markdown checkbox scope that defines executable task exhaustion; checkpoint sign-offs, acceptance lists, and other checkboxes are evidence or presentation, not task identities. A legacy whole-document fallback is retained only for documents without an explicit ledger.

records.summary: Recover stale implementation authority or pause unchanged host transitions for a user decision
records.whyHappened: FEAT-070 Phase 6 completed both declared tasks and passed the repaired full-verification profile, but its Quality Gate Evidence table also contained a non-blocking Test coverage row with a missing outcome. The reconciliation adapter classified every label containing the word test as the blocking Tests gate, so the later coverage row overwrote the valid Tests decision. The policy then selected the already-checked final verification task as a supposed recovery route. Worker entry correctly refused to execute completed work, pre-review selected the same checked task again, and the autonomous coordinator had no no-progress bound tied to durable state.
records.causalChain: Full verification passed and checked the final task -> coverage telemetry remained unavailable/non-blocking -> substring gate normalization mapped Test coverage to Tests -> reconciliation reported a recoverable missing Tests gate -> policy returned select with the last checked task ID without invalidating it -> worker entry observed every task complete -> pre-review requested the same phase -> no FEAT/task/review/checkpoint evidence changed -> the host repeated the route thousands of times, consumed CPU, and grew progress logs without launching Pi.
records.testGap: Adapter tests had no Quality Gate Evidence table containing both blocking Tests and advisory Test coverage rows. Policy tests asserted that a missing gate should select an already-checked task but never proved that the task could actually become executable. Coordinator tests covered individual repeats but had no unchanged before-and-after fingerprint scenario, no blocked-awaiting-user assertion, and no failure-brief classification for host no-progress pausing.
records.missingDecision: The missing invariant was that advisory coverage is not a blocking gate namespace, and a checked task cannot be returned as executable recovery work without an authoritative invalidation mutation. Every repeated host route must demonstrate durable FEAT/task/review/checkpoint progress. If one recovery cycle returns to an identical route, decision, and fingerprint, evidence proves no progress without an arbitrary count: the workflow pauses as blocked, publishes exact guidance, preserves completed work, and waits for the user to choose Continue Implementation or Cancel.

records.summary: Separate direct-host model authority from explicit orchestrated action admission
records.whyHappened: The original EPIC-011 runtime treated a direct Pi skill invocation as a candidate orchestrated launch and compared its current route with Hepha policy. Command-name helpers and a command-conditioned implementation route bundle also allowed workflow labels to become action authority before the registered launch boundary. During the corrective cutover, the complete registry-plan predicate was composed into specialist and implementation workers but generic task and nested adapters retained a reduced action-ID-only check.
records.causalChain: A user selected a host model -> invoked a portable skill -> DirectSessionHandoffAdapter queried Hepha policy -> a mismatch created a second worker and orchestrated receipt; separately, a workflow command string entered actionForWorkflowCommand/getImplementationRoutes -> inferred an action bundle -> resolved plans before an explicit dispatch action was admitted. The first cutover then validated complete plans at only two consumers -> another structurally valid plan could conflict in type, role, prompt, or capability metadata -> generic task storage or nested coordinator execution could begin under incomplete registry authority.
records.testGap: FEAT-062 proved pinned Pi routes, secret isolation, fallback, recovery, and direct mismatch transfer, but its direct scenario encoded the wrong transfer requirement. It had no Pi/Codex/Claude direct-host fixture, no complete portable production-asset admission, and no generic missing/unknown/conflicting action control that asserted zero resolver and runtime calls. Initial FEAT-071 tests mutated only plan action ID at generic and nested boundaries; they did not mutate action type, role, prompt version, or each capability independently through both public adapters, and the constructor audit did not require the shared complete predicate at every consumer.
records.missingDecision: Execution mode is selected only by the entry point. Direct-host work never enters orchestrated routing. Every orchestrated root or nested launch admits one explicit top-level agent_action, checks registry and launch-node equality before resolution, and requires action ID, action type, role ID, prompt version, minimum context window, requiresApi, requiresReasoning, and requiresTools to equal one registry entry before storage, coordinator work, or spawn. Command names, filenames, roles, skill metadata, models, and route fields are never action authority.

records.summary: Persist direct-host state-sync evidence without creating route authority
records.whyHappened: The routed FEAT-062 receipt tables could represent only orchestrated attempts. Direct procedures either had no durable execution record or were forced through the now-removed mismatch-transfer concept, so state sync and honest unrecorded host-model evidence had no route-incapable authority.
records.causalChain: A direct host procedure completed deterministic state sync -> the only runtime store required an approved plan, route, authentication, attempts, and an orchestrated invocation identity -> direct work could not be represented without fabricating policy facts or remaining invisible -> FEAT Details could not distinguish a direct unobserved model from legacy activity.
records.testGap: Earlier unit and browser evidence exercised orchestrated chains and legacy Not recorded presentation but had no generic public composition scenario that persisted direct state-sync evidence, reopened it by identity, joined both authorities, or rejected a direct record contaminated by an orchestrated policy field.
records.missingDecision: Direct-host evidence is a separate exact-key SQLite authority. It may record deterministic state sync and explicitly trusted observed model provenance, but it cannot represent route, policy, launch, authentication, credential, attempt, or fallback facts. Exact replay is a no-op, identity collision rejects, both stores validate independently before membership filtering, and the public phase page uses one explicit ordered execution-mode union.

records.summary: Make authoritative fixer successor shape explicit and retries actionable
records.whyHappened: The fixer prompt showed empty findingResponses/itemReceipts/testReceipts arrays and expected the model to infer the nested V1 contract. The fixer repeatedly emitted obsolete summary fields such as fixerDecision, remediatedItemIds, and completedTestIds. Authoritative ingress correctly rejected that payload, but collapsed the validator result to the generic message that the input was invalid, so every same-phase retry reproduced the same payload.
records.causalChain: NEEDS_CHANGES manifest dispatched fixer -> fixer completed code and tests -> fixer emitted a non-canonical remediation response -> V1 validator returned invalid_shape -> integration erased the rejection detail -> repair prompt said only input is invalid -> fixer reused the same report JSON -> repeated fixer attempts never persisted the response/receipt -> independent reviewer was never eligible to run.
records.testGap: Prompt tests asserted headings and placeholders but not the nested response item fields or receipt entry fields. Successor ingestion tests checked refusal codes but did not prove that the safe validator code/message reached the same-fixer repair brief for the obsolete payload shape observed in a real run.
records.missingDecision: The fixer must append or update exactly one Fixer Response section in the existing NEEDS_CHANGES report and must not replace reviewer-owned text or create a fixer-authored review decision. The prompt must publish the complete canonical nested schema and explicitly separate human Markdown Fixer Decision fields from V1 remediation item fields. Authoritative ingress remains strict and performs no normalization, but a validator rejection must retain its sanitized contract code/message so the bounded retry can correct the payload. Only a persisted response plus bound receipt enables the independent reviewer rerun, which creates a new APPROVED or NEEDS_CHANGES report.

records.summary: Preserve primary provider failure while a mutation-owning fallback completes
records.whyHappened: A valid active DeepSeek Pi-session connection was cataloged at api.deepseek.com, but runtime provider mapping recognized Pi-session connections only when they were the single installation default. Because OpenAI/Codex was the installation default, DeepSeek resolved to null and the primary attempt safely failed provider_unsupported before spawn. The coordinator then launched the approved GPT fallback without passing attempt lifecycle hooks, so the mutation tracker retained no current fallback attempt identity and rejected the first write with RUNTIME_PERSISTENCE_FAILED.
records.causalChain: DeepSeek route selected -> pi_session was not the OpenAI installation-default connection -> provider mapper returned null -> durable primary failure provider_unsupported with work state none -> coordinator legally selected GPT fallback -> fallback process ran but beforeProcess hook was omitted -> first fallback write could not bind work state to the fallback attempt -> runtime killed a healthy fallback and failed the phase.
records.testGap: The existing fallback integration returned plain text and performed no write/edit event. Coordinator tests proved route selection but did not prove that attempt lifecycle hooks were invoked for the second attempt. Provider tests mapped the DeepSeek endpoint for discovery but did not exercise runtime provider resolution for a non-default Pi-session connection. Presentation tests showed a generic fallback but did not explicitly assert a provider_unsupported primary beside a completed fallback.
records.missingDecision: A unique code-owned Pi-session endpoint is sufficient runtime provider authority even when it is not the installation default; ambiguous endpoints still require explicit default disambiguation. Primary and fallback attempts keep separate lifecycle identities. The primary failure remains durable as the route-change reason, fallback mutations/checkpoints bind only to the fallback attempt, and a completed fallback completes the invocation and phase worker successfully. Only a failed fallback makes the invocation fail.

records.summary: Prefer a writable fork for unconfigured phase checkpoint publication
records.whyHappened: A completed phase checkpoint selected origin whenever the feature branch had no configured upstream. In a repository where origin is a read-only upstream and fork is the authenticated contributor remote, the push failed with HTTP 403 and left the phase checkpoint pending despite a valid local commit.
records.causalChain: Phase checkpoint loaded an unconfigured feature branch -> selectPushRemote preferred origin whenever it existed -> push attempted the upstream remote rather than the writable fork -> publication failed -> WF-PHASE-GIT-PENDING stopped later phase selection.
records.testGap: Remote-selection tests covered only repositories with origin as the sole remote. No unit policy matrix represented configured branch remotes, a fork plus upstream-origin topology, or an ambiguous multi-remote topology; no Gherkin route proved that checkpoint publication leaves origin untouched when fork is selected. Recovery coverage also assumed a clean worktree, so an unrelated later-phase edit incorrectly prevented publication of an already sealed checkpoint.
records.missingDecision: The checkpoint contract lacked a generic remote-selection invariant for contributor forks. A valid configured branch remote must remain authoritative; otherwise a named fork is preferred over origin, a sole remote is accepted, and any other multiple-remote topology is rejected rather than guessing a publication target. A sealed checkpoint retry must verify that each immutable commit remains reachable from a current feature branch, then push without staging the worktree; unrelated later work is not checkpoint authority and must remain unstaged.

records.summary: Reject contract-to-ledger drift before generic phase dispatch
records.whyHappened: An ordered phase contract declared two executable tasks while its explicit Markdown ledger also contained uncontracted descriptive checkboxes. The worker queue selected only the two contract tasks, but phase completion required every ledger checkbox to be checked, so completed work reached phase exit and was incorrectly rejected as unresolved.
records.causalChain: Refinement/template alignment rendered descriptive work as ledger checkboxes -> contract-task projection ignored entries without a contract ID -> both declared tasks completed durably -> completion read the broader ledger state -> an extra unchecked checkbox denied phase exit after work had already run.
records.testGap: Validation covered missing, unknown, reordered, and incorrectly checked contract markers, while task projection filtered non-contract entries. No unit, Gherkin, or dashboard journey created an extra uncontracted checkbox inside an explicit V3 ledger and required rejection before dispatch, visible blocked readiness, and no lifecycle side effects. The first admission correction also lacked a valid V3 continuation counterpart, which allowed the valid-validator branch to be treated as missing artifacts whenever a contract existed.
records.missingDecision: V3 lacked the explicit invariant that PhaseExecutionContract.json is the machine sequence authority and the Phase Task Ledger is an exact durable projection: same count, order, contract IDs, and executors. The system also trusted a prior artifact-readiness projection instead of revalidating a live V3 contract at Start and Continue admission. Live validation is fail-closed only when invalid: a valid contract must not manufacture a missing-artifact blocker.

records.summary: Enforce data-boundary immutability pattern: validate DTO invariants at construction, not in downstream functions
records.whyHappened: PhaseReviewResumePlanningInput allowed awaitingIndependentRerun: true to coexist with nextOrderedTaskKind: "code_review" and no prior review evidence. The downstream planner received an impossible state and silently favoured rerun over baseline. The rerun executor then correctly rejected the request because no prior review artifact existed. The defect was not in the rerun executor, which correctly failed closed, but in the DTO boundary that allowed the impossible combination to propagate.
records.causalChain: Session text created rerun state -> no scoped boundary validated the combination -> planner received both rerun and baseline flags true -> rerun precedence made the decision -> rerun executor correctly found no lineage -> phase failed with REVIEW_CONTRACT_V1_RERUN_LINEAGE_UNAVAILABLE
records.testGap: The planner and rerun executor had individual tests. No test proved that awaitingIndependentRerun and nextOrderedTaskKind: code_review cannot be true simultaneously when no prior review evidence exists. The Gherkin invariant was absent.
records.missingDecision: DTOs that carry lifecycle state must validate their invariants at construction. Downstream functions must never correct impossible state — the DTO boundary must make it structurally impossible. Immutability (readonly fields) and a factory function are the mechanism.

records.summary: Add an explicit legacy MCP recipe-source compatibility boundary
records.whyHappened: Native Hepha attempted to migrate proven DevCycle recipe behavior and deterministic lifecycle authority at the same time. Repeated failures could not distinguish a recipe defect from strict Markdown parsing, V3 artifact projection, phase routing, runtime dispatch, or model execution defects because there was no way to hold every shared runtime variable constant while changing only recipe authority.
records.causalChain: Legacy MCP workflow worked in direct clients -> Hepha copied and expanded its instructions into native applications -> native lifecycle gates and generated document contracts evolved together -> failures crossed several boundaries -> fixes overfit individual observed output instead of isolating whether the recipe or shared executor was responsible.
records.testGap: No unit or Gherkin scenario selected between proven MCP and native recipe authority for the same action identity, asserted that invalid source configuration fails at construction, proved one selected model receives an MCP-enabled invocation, or preserved native Hepha as the default rollback path.
records.missingDecision: Recipe authority must be an explicit validated operation-level input. A compatibility run must bypass native lifecycle post-processing so the MCP/native comparison changes one variable, while model selection, Pi execution, telemetry, project identity, and user-visible action identity remain shared.

records.summary: Make unresolved validation markers the sole Deep-Dive readiness authority
records.whyHappened: The dashboard projected implementation and refinement outputs, Deep-Dive receipt history, and source-hash freshness as clarification prerequisites for newly submitted FEATs. Linking phases or making other marker-free lifecycle edits therefore appeared to require another Deep-Dive even though no unresolved decision existed.
records.causalChain: one aggregate readiness evaluator served every lifecycle action -> submitted cards ran future artifact validators -> hash mismatch and absent receipt became blocking Deep-Dive reasons -> dashboard mixed those reasons with explicit validation markers -> users were asked to recreate files or repeat clarification before the operations that produce those files
records.testGap: No acceptance test proved that a submitted FEAT with zero validation markers remains clarification-ready when metadata is absent, its file hash changes, or future refinement artifacts do not exist. Continue also retained an unconditional source-hash recovery call.
records.missingDecision: Deep-Dive is required if and only if the authoritative description contains an unresolved validation marker. Marker-free file changes, phase-link updates, metadata availability, historical receipts, and source hashes are audit context rather than workflow authority. Submitted readiness must not validate outputs of later actions.

records.summary: Close implementation decisions in Deep-Dive and prohibit deferred human gates
records.whyHappened: A DevCycle-refined feature entered Phase 1 with a task requiring product/platform owner attestation and CODEOWNER approval. Autonomous Continue correctly read the task literally and stopped repeatedly, even though implementation should have received all product decisions from Deep-Dive and should own technical decision, automated review, and acceptance execution.
records.causalChain: Deep-Dive question planning used markers plus an arbitrary fallback count and allowed FEAT decisions to be deferred -> Refine had no invariant or artifact check forbidding human-sign-off tasks -> the MCP compatibility wrapper treated provider prose as unconstrained lifecycle authority -> Continue interpreted the generated owner-attestation task as a valid human blocker -> autonomous execution terminated without code work.
records.testGap: No Deep-Dive prompt test required exhaustive implementation-decision closure, no fallback-option test prohibited deferral to refinement, no DevCycle refinement validator rejected a human-sign-off task, no compatibility-prompt test asserted delegated autonomous decision authority, and continuation readiness had no provider-specific in-progress artifact fixture.
records.missingDecision: Deep-Dive owns target ambiguity closure; Refine must publish only tasks executable by an autonomous developer; autonomous and single-phase workers are delegated decision authority and invoke automated review/acceptance; provider ownership selects artifact validation without weakening lifecycle invariants.

records.summary: Separate current-action readiness from Complete Feature readiness
records.whyHappened: An in-progress FEAT in Phase 1 exposed Continue Implementing, but the detail blade labelled the overall workflow blocked and rendered native structural errors from every future phase. A board badge also treated missing evidence from an already completed early phase as a current implementation blocker.
records.causalChain: one readiness field carried preparation, continuation, and structural completion diagnostics -> MCP action availability correctly bypassed native continuation gates -> presentation independently rendered the stale blocking list -> the UI contradicted its enabled Continue action -> completion-only quality evidence appeared as a board-level current blocker.
records.testGap: No projection test required readiness to become ready when MCP Continue is available, no presentation test separated Current workflow from Complete Feature readiness, no mapper test suppressed completion-only blockers during continuation, and no board test limited quality-gap badges to implementation-complete features.
records.missingDecision: Readiness is action-scoped. Current workflow reflects the action that can run now; Complete Feature has an independent finalization projection. Future phase and final quality obligations may block completion later but cannot label an available Continue action blocked.

records.summary: Attribute AI execution time and command models to implementation phases
records.whyHappened: The FEAT timing summary counted DevCycle MCP Start and Continue workers, but each phase row said Legacy activity / Not recorded because compatibility workers were persisted without phase identity. Phase rows also omitted the model selected by the orchestrator command.
records.causalChain: the MCP compatibility boundary dispatched implementation workers with null phase metadata -> agent executions contributed only to the feature aggregate -> phase timing read only phase-run records -> partial Phase 1 work and completed Phase 0 work showed no AI time -> the worker persisted not-recorded instead of the immutable command-plan model -> the operator could not audit which model the orchestrator commanded.
records.testGap: No compatibility application test required Start/Continue dispatch to bind the first unresolved lifecycle phase, no worker test required persistence of the command-plan model, no presentation test summed settled agent attempts for an in-progress phase, and no legacy reconciliation test covered pre-fix MCP records.
records.missingDecision: Every implementation dispatch owns a phase telemetry scope selected from lifecycle state, settled agent attempts accumulate before phase completion, autonomous cross-phase sessions are segmented by durable phase-artifact update boundaries, and completed/in-progress phases retain expandable orchestrator runtime evidence. The command-plan model is displayed as intent while observed/fallback routing remains separate evidence.

records.summary: Replace the implementation completion deadline with progress-based liveness
records.whyHappened: Implementation workers inherited a repository-default 30-minute wall-clock maximum even though autonomous feature work can remain productive for several hours. One worker completed multiple phases, entered the next phase, continued emitting tool and Pi output, and was killed at exactly 1,800 seconds despite active progress.
records.causalChain: the implementation profile supplied both a resettable idle timer and a fixed default total timer -> every stdout and stderr event correctly reset idle liveness -> the independent wall-clock timer never reset -> productive work crossed the 30-minute boundary -> Hepha terminated Pi mid-task and projected a recovery-required workflow failure
records.testGap: The runner tests proved that callers could explicitly disable a maximum and that continuing activity did not bypass an explicit maximum, but no test required the implementation profile's repository default itself to disable the maximum. Runtime-settings tests asserted numeric values without distinguishing inactivity from total duration, and no generic Gherkin scenario defined productive multi-hour implementation liveness.
records.missingDecision: Implementation completion duration is not a safety contract. The repository default must use one resettable no-progress stall circuit driven by observable current-worker output, process liveness alone must not reset it, and a wall-clock maximum may exist only as explicit operator policy.

records.summary: Keep manual verification available after provider-owned feature completion
records.whyHappened: The native workflow originally kept a feature in 03_IN_PROGRESS until manual review and manual tests were recorded. A compatibility provider now legitimately executes its own Complete Feature procedure and moves the FEAT to 04_COMPLETED before Hepha's local manual verification pack is generated. The workflow projector restricted pack generation and human evidence to 03_IN_PROGRESS, leaving the completed card's Generate Test Pack action disabled even though the adapter and SQLite store could operate on the completed folder.
records.causalChain: manual verification eligibility was coupled to the pre-completion folder -> the provider completed and archived the FEAT in one autonomous call -> implementation evidence remained resolved and the Manual Tests panel remained visible -> the projector returned canGenerateManualTestPack false solely because the folder was 04_COMPLETED -> the user could not create or record post-completion evidence
records.testGap: Manual verification tests covered unresolved rejection and the in-progress all-pass transition into Complete Feature, but no generic scenario projected a completed FEAT or required an all-pass result to avoid starting Complete Feature twice.
records.missingDecision: Feature completion is not a filesystem freeze and manual verification is an independent SQLite-authoritative evidence dimension. Completed FEATs may create derived pack documents, record findings, and become manual-tests green without changing lifecycle folder or depending on the implementation recipe provider.

records.summary: Resolve authenticated Pi providers and explain route exhaustion
records.whyHappened: Refine Feature selected the available OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol route, but the OpenAI endpoint represents both openai and openai-codex while Pi's explicit installation default was DeepSeek. Runtime provider resolution therefore failed closed as provider_unsupported before process spawn. The workflow collapsed the durable attempt cause into RUNTIME_ROUTE_SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED, so the detail blade showed neither the failed route nor a viable recovery action, and retrying the unchanged route deterministically failed again.
records.causalChain: available catalog route selected -> endpoint exposed multiple code-owned provider identities -> route did not match the installation default -> provider resolver ignored the uniquely authenticated openai-codex identity -> primary preparation failed provider_unsupported with no fallback -> prompt runner discarded the durable attempt cause -> UI showed only sequence exhausted
records.testGap: Provider resolution tests covered installation-default OpenAI and unique DeepSeek endpoints but not an ambiguous endpoint with exactly one authenticated Pi provider. Worker integration tests asserted durable provider_unsupported evidence with a successful fallback but did not require a no-fallback error to expose route, cause, fallback state, and recovery guidance.
records.missingDecision: For a Pi-session endpoint with multiple code-owned provider identities, exactly one identity present in Pi authentication state is sufficient runtime authority when the installation default does not identify that connection. Credential values remain private. Zero or multiple matches fail closed. Exhaustion errors must present durable attempt evidence and an actionable routing recovery rather than only the coordinator's aggregate code.

records.summary: Turn incomplete MCP refinement into interactive Deep-Dive recovery
records.whyHappened: Two MCP Refine workers correctly refused to publish artifacts because the generated FEAT still lacked concrete scope and acceptance criteria. The compatibility application treated a zero-exit Pi process as action completion, populated refineCompletedAt, and projected every workflow node completed even though the FEAT remained submitted with no artifacts. The worker summary contained actionable Deep-Dive questions, but no open Deep-Dive session or recovery action was exposed because the earlier fallback had consumed the source markers.
records.causalChain: placeholder FEAT entered Deep-Dive -> failed document rewrite appended generic Accept current decisions and consumed markers -> MCP Refine discovered unresolved target decisions -> worker exited normally without artifacts -> compatibility boundary equated process success with lifecycle completion -> completed metadata hid the blocked result transition -> marker-only recovery presentation offered Refine again instead of Deep-Dive
records.testGap: Compatibility tests asserted only worker dispatch and process completion; they did not require Ready To Develop state plus complete provider artifacts before recording refinement complete. Projection tests did not reconcile false completed metadata, and presentation tests required source markers even when the current Refine action had discovered a new target decision.
records.missingDecision: Model-process completion and workflow-action completion are separate. MCP refinement completes only when provider-independent postconditions are true. A current blocked Refine result may authorize the normal Deep-Dive recovery after earlier source markers were consumed; historical receipts and hashes still do not create readiness requirements.

records.summary: Keep productive Deep-Dive question discovery alive and reject synthetic fallback rounds
records.whyHappened: A comprehensive FEAT question worker spent three minutes reading the target, parent EPIC, related features, architecture, design baselines, and source code, but the generic 180-second prompt maximum killed it while productive. DeepDiveQuestionPlanner caught that failure and silently replaced the unfinished analysis with three generic User workflow, Acceptance criteria, and Feature boundaries questions whose recommended option was Accept current. Those questions repeated the earlier invalid fallback and could falsely close an underspecified target.
records.causalChain: comprehensive question discovery required broad evidence -> worker emitted continuing tool progress -> absolute generic prompt timeout ignored that progress -> model process was killed before its JSON manifest -> planner treated failure as permission to synthesize generic questions -> UI presented the synthetic round as agent-finished authoritative decisions
records.testGap: Question-planner tests expected local fallback after every model failure and asserted a fixed timeoutMs option. No test required no absolute maximum, a progress inactivity circuit, or visible failure instead of synthetic clarification authority.
records.missingDecision: Deep-Dive question discovery follows progress-based liveness. Productive work may exceed the old generic duration; inactivity still stops a stalled worker. Failed, empty, or malformed model analysis cannot be replaced by generic decisions and must follow the durable Deep-Dive failure path for explicit retry.

records.summary: Discover ordered acceptance criteria and keep TestPack failures visible
records.whyHappened: FEAT-002 completed with twenty-seven concrete numbered acceptance criteria. TestPack source discovery recognized only dash or asterisk list items, so generation found no source items and returned HTTP 400. The action controller swallowed the rejected request after sending the error to a global surface hidden behind the modal, refreshed the unchanged missing status, and made the button appear to do nothing. Missing pack status also projected a PDF link because optional chaining produced undefined and the policy compared it only with null.
records.causalChain: provider authored ordered acceptance criteria -> unordered-only extractor returned an empty manifest -> generation failed before durable pack creation -> HTTP response exposed message but not the web client's safe error field -> controller consumed the exception -> modal retained only missing status -> undefined PDF path compared unequal to null -> invalid PDF links remained visible
records.testGap: Source-discovery tests covered only unordered acceptance criteria. Missing-status tests asserted the message but not artifact-link flags. Panel integration asserted that the generation button existed but never exercised a failed click or required its reason to remain inside the dialog.
records.missingDecision: Supported acceptance sections may use ordered, unordered, or checkbox criteria and each item is extracted exactly once. Failed manual-verification actions must return a safe actionable error, reject through the controller, and render that reason inside the still-open dialog. Missing packs project no artifact links.

records.summary: Preserve complete Deep-Dive manifests and expose long-running generation honestly
records.whyHappened: The FEAT-003 question worker performed productive research for about eight minutes and returned twenty-eight concrete vault, cryptography, lifecycle, compatibility, and acceptance decisions. The parser silently sliced every valid manifest to eight questions, contradicting the prompt's no-arbitrary-count contract and discarding twenty decisions. During research the overlay showed only an indefinite spinner, so productive output looked frozen even while the worker stream grew continuously.
records.causalChain: question prompt required complete decision closure -> worker inspected authoritative dependencies and emitted 28 valid questions -> parser retained only the first 8 through a legacy presentation cap -> SQLite persisted the truncated round -> UI represented the 8 as complete authority -> generation overlay exposed neither elapsed time nor safe background continuation
records.testGap: The parser test explicitly required truncation to eight rather than proving complete coverage preservation. The overlay test asserted only a generating label and disabled button, not elapsed/background liveness guidance.
records.missingDecision: Question-count limits cannot override decision closure. Every structurally valid model-generated question must be persisted. Long productive generation remains progress-monitored and the dialog must show elapsed time, explain background continuation, and distinguish a progress stall from duration alone.

records.summary: Evaluate every Deep-Dive answer with an adaptive follow-up turn
records.whyHappened: The direct FEAT-003 interview reached thirty-nine questions because each answer exposed dependent cryptographic, credential-admission, record-layout, and lifecycle decisions. Hepha generated a broad initial manifest but treated it as a closed queue, so saving an option could never ask the next answer-dependent question and the final static answer could authorize document update without an adaptive closure audit.
records.causalChain: initial source analysis generated independent and anticipated decisions -> user selected a concrete option -> session application marked only that static row answered -> no model evaluated the answer consequence -> dependent decisions remained absent -> all static rows could become ready_for_update despite an incomplete interview branch
records.testGap: Session tests required the final static answer to become ready immediately and had no follow-up planner, parent linkage, insertion ordering, no-tools follow-up route, failure boundary, or adaptive UI state.
records.missingDecision: The default Hepha interview starts with exactly one highest-priority opening question rather than waiting for a static complete batch. Every saved answer is durable before evaluation and then receives one immediate no-tools adaptive interviewer turn using the authoritative source and full transcript. A dependent question is inserted directly after its parent and traced by parentQuestionId. The final pending answer is also a closure audit. Follow-up failure fails closed and cannot authorize document update.

records.summary: Keep Refine Feature documentation-only and statically discover quality commands
records.whyHappened: FEAT-005 refinement was collecting repository and dependency context when the planning worker emitted cargo search and cargo version probes in one shell turn. Hepha correctly blocked multiple Cargo commands, but the action then exhausted its route despite refinement requiring only documents, manifests, lockfiles, and a plan.
records.causalChain: refinement recipe requested technology and command discovery -> worker treated discovery as permission to execute package-manager probes -> one turn emitted multiple Cargo commands -> implementation command-safety policy blocked the call -> no refinement artifacts were created -> runtime route sequence exhausted even though the FEAT had no unresolved decisions
records.testGap: The MCP compatibility prompt tested decision ownership and postconditions but did not prohibit executing builds, tests, compilers, package registries, or toolchain probes during documentation-only refinement.
records.missingDecision: Refine Feature discovers stack and quality commands statically from manifests, lockfiles, workflows, source, and documentation. It records commands without running them, does not mutate product implementation repositories, and may use documentation research when static evidence is insufficient.

records.summary: Put Cargo serialization and zero-warning authority in every implementation dispatch
records.whyHappened: The FEAT-005 implementation worker twice described a single Cargo command but appended cargo --version or cargo test to the same shell call. Hepha blocked both requests correctly, yet each violation terminated an otherwise productive autonomous run. The same worker also marked thirteen lint warnings and a static-build warning green as pre-existing or benign despite the configured zero-warning contract.
records.causalChain: Cargo discipline existed in repository lessons and the runtime safety monitor -> implementation dispatch prompt did not repeat the exact turn-scoped shape -> model generated two Cargo invocations in one shell tool call -> monitor prevented execution -> run stopped at a recovery checkpoint -> quality narration separately treated warning-bearing exit-zero commands as green
records.testGap: Compatibility prompt tests covered autonomy and human-gate removal but did not require exactly one Cargo invocation per assistant turn or assert that warning-bearing exit-zero gates remain red.
records.missingDecision: Every implementation dispatch explicitly states that one assistant turn may contain one tool call with exactly one Cargo invocation, whose result must be inspected before a later Cargo command. Every configured warning remains red regardless of exit code, age, or worker classification.

records.summary: Move Cargo sequencing authority from unconditional dispatch to conditional refinement output
records.whyHappened: The first correction repeated Cargo instructions in every implementation dispatch. That protected FEAT-005 but exposed non-Rust projects to an irrelevant technology-specific recommendation and bypassed Refine Feature's responsibility to derive execution constraints from the actual target stack.
records.causalChain: FEAT-005 used the existing Tauri Rust target -> Cargo commands required serialized execution -> the rule was added globally to compatibility dispatch -> every project received Cargo prose regardless of its stack -> the overfitting was identified -> Cargo activation moved to static refinement evidence and inherited phase artifacts
records.testGap: Dispatch tests asserted unconditional Cargo wording and did not prove that non-Cargo projects avoid Cargo-specific instructions or that refinement requires both a target Cargo.toml and feature-level Cargo usage.
records.missingDecision: Refine Feature emits the Rust/Cargo sequential profile only when both activation conditions are proven, writes activation evidence to FeatureTasks and every phase, and splits Cargo gates into ordered commands. Implementation dispatch applies only inherited stack constraints and remains technology-neutral. Universal zero-warning authority is unchanged.

records.summary: Permit sequential foreground Cargo invocations while retaining concurrency protection
records.whyHappened: FEAT-005 workers repeatedly followed the one-invocation rule for many commands and later combined two read-only Cargo diagnostics sequentially in one shell call. The host guard terminated the productive worker even though no Cargo processes would have overlapped, showing that the one-invocation policy was stricter than the underlying shared-target safety requirement.
records.causalChain: Cargo target contention motivated serialization -> serialization was implemented as one invocation per tool call -> a worker emitted sequential foreground Cargo commands -> the guard treated sequencing as concurrency -> the run terminated despite no background process -> policy narrowed to actual background, sibling, active-call, and timeout hazards
records.testGap: Tool-safety tests treated every multi-invocation shell command as unsafe and did not distinguish `&&` or `;` sequencing from `&` background execution or sibling tool-call concurrency.
records.missingDecision: Sequential Cargo invocations are permitted in one foreground shell tool call. Cargo may not be backgrounded, emitted through sibling tool calls that Pi executes concurrently, or started while a prior Cargo call remains active. Timeout process inspection and zero-warning authority remain mandatory.

records.summary: Separate implementation completion from external release readiness
records.whyHappened: FEAT-007 completed every client-owned task and all executable client gates, but the compatibility worker kept Phase 8 incomplete because separately owned server hardening, future server TwinTests, and physical-platform qualification evidence were unavailable. Repeated Continue actions deterministically rediscovered the same findings and stopped without actionable in-scope recovery work.
records.causalChain: refinement copied release dependencies into the final checkpoint -> implementation completed its owned work -> final worker treated missing external evidence as implementation failure authority -> Hepha projected implementation stopped and offered Continue -> Continue re-read unchanged external findings -> the run stopped again despite no in-scope red gate
records.testGap: Compatibility prompt tests enforced clean configured commands and autonomous decision ownership but did not state that implementation completion and release readiness are independent or prohibit external release findings from keeping a phase incomplete.
records.missingDecision: Only unresolved in-scope tasks and configured executable gates owned by the current feature can block implementation acceptance. Separately owned repository work, future suites, physical qualification, deployment certification, and organizational release evidence are recorded in the final report, FeatureDescription, linked epic, and Lessons Learned with recommended follow-up EPIC/FEAT work. A feature may be Implementation COMPLETED while Release Readiness remains BLOCKED_BY_EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES.

records.summary: Defer non-automatable tasks into mandatory Manual TestPack obligations
records.whyHappened: A physical-platform qualification task could not execute in the autonomous environment. The worker first treated unavailable targets as a phase blocker and a later repair incorrectly marked the task COMPLETED, even though no physical test had run. That erased the audit distinction between implemented automation, skipped autonomous work, and pending user verification.
records.causalChain: Refinement authored physical qualification as an executable implementation gate -> Start preserved it as PENDING -> Continue could not supply the physical target -> provider stopped the phase -> one-off recovery changed the task to COMPLETED -> no durable skip receipt or generated Manual TestPack obligation proved that user testing remained pending
records.testGap: Refinement tests did not classify automation feasibility, phase-worker settlement had no immutable manual-deferral result, MCP recipes allowed direct status mutation, and Manual TestPack discovery did not consume skipped implementation tasks.
records.missingDecision: Refine classifies each test as AUTOMATABLE or MANUAL_TEST_REQUIRED. Manual-only tasks are SKIPPED with the exact canonical reason and a durable ManualTestObligations.json procedure. Runtime discovery uses HEPHA_MANUAL_TEST_DEFERRAL_V1; HEPHA alone writes SQLite and Markdown state. The generated pack must contain every obligation. Pending manual results block release readiness, never implementation completion, while actually executed red commands remain blocking.

records.summary: Bind DevCycle manual-test obligations to durable phase-ledger identity before Start
records.whyHappened: A DevCycle refinement correctly classified two physical qualification tasks as SKIPPED and emitted ManualTestObligations.json, but represented the tasks only through numbered Markdown headings and status prose. Start correctly refused to seed either obligation because neither task ID resolved to a HEPHA phase-ledger item.
records.causalChain: DevCycle prompt requested a stable phase/task source but no durable checkbox binding -> worker invented phase-7-task identifiers in ManualTestObligations.json -> provider-specific refinement validation checked phase files and statuses but not obligation-to-ledger traceability -> FEAT moved to Ready -> Start fail-closed seeding found zero matching ledger tasks -> no implementation workflow started
records.testGap: V3 refinement tests covered execution-contract task identity and Start tests covered an injected seeding failure, but no generic DevCycle refinement test paired a legacy contract-marked checkbox with ManualTestObligations.json or rejected an orphaned obligation before Ready promotion. Seeding tests also did not prove that persistence preserves the stable contract task ID instead of replacing it with the derived Markdown ledger ID.
records.missingDecision: Provider choice cannot weaken manual-test traceability. Every DevCycle manual-only task must project one durable checkbox beginning with [contract:<taskId>], and the obligation must reuse that exact unique ID and phase projection. Provider-specific refinement validation rejects missing, duplicate, ambiguous, or cross-phase bindings. Start records the derived SQLite ledger task separately while preserving contract identity in the durable obligation.

records.summary: Classify test delivery and reject fabricated manual-test readiness
records.whyHappened: Manual-pack generation treated every discovered acceptance criterion as a request for a human test and synthesized the same generic navigation/workflow/check instruction even for backend-only domain work. The dashboard independently treated the presence of a generated PDF as readiness, while automated command outcomes treated exit code zero as passing without checking whether any test matched.
records.causalChain: Acceptance discovery found 26 FEAT-012 domain criteria -> the generator manufactured one placeholder manual case per criterion -> coverage could not bind those cases and reported every criterion Missing -> PDF generation still created a current artifact -> the dashboard equated current artifact state with Manual Test Pack Ready -> a non-executable package appeared releasable despite having no valid manual surface
records.testGap: Tests asserted deterministic generation and artifact lifecycle but did not cover a backend-only feature, a mixed manual/automated feature, placeholder rejection, the invariant that readiness requires a valid case, or an exit-zero command reporting no matching tests.
records.missingDecision: The workflow lacked a criterion-level Manual/Automated/Deferred/Uncovered classification and a single readiness invariant shared by generation, validation, review, and presentation. Manual cases now require explicit obligations with a named interface, preconditions, setup data, executable actions, and observable results. No valid case means Not Applicable when all criteria have automated or deferred evidence, otherwise Incomplete. Automated execution separately records passed, failed, zero tests discovered, and not executed.

records.summary: Unify provider-owned refinement validation across promotion, readiness, and implementation admission
records.whyHappened: A compatibility refinement worker could exit successfully and move a feature into Ready To Develop even when its provider-owned artifacts violated the provider contract. The dashboard then evaluated the same files with the native artifact validator while its MCP action path bypassed readiness entirely. Direct Start reached a third implicit validator inside manual-test seeding and failed on a task identity reconstructed from prose.
records.causalChain: recipe selection chose a provider-specific output format -> Refine completion checked lifecycle placement and file presence but not the provider contract -> the board applied a different native validator yet enabled MCP Start from the folder alone -> direct Start skipped artifact admission -> manual-test recovery attempted to infer stable identity from a numbered heading -> zero matches caused a late failure after the feature had already appeared ready
records.testGap: Compatibility tests covered successful dispatch and provider-format validation independently, but did not prove that invalid terminal refinement output fails promotion, that dashboard and direct execution share the same selected validator, or that rejected Start produces no workflow, worker, or manual-test side effects. Deferred-decision validation also covered a positive human gate but not negated policy statements that explicitly prohibit one.
records.missingDecision: Recipe selection now selects one authoritative artifact validator for the entire action boundary. Refine validates provider output before reporting completion. Dashboard readiness and direct Start/Continue admission use that same validator. Invalid Ready artifacts keep Refine available with deterministic repair diagnostics, while implementation admission fails before any side effect. Manual obligations must bind through unique [contract:<taskId>] ledger markers; prose headings are never identity.

records.summary: Own compatibility session continuation, lifecycle projection, and truthful recovery outcomes
records.whyHappened: A successful autonomous worker returned after several accepted phases because it preferred a fresh session budget. HEPHA marked the workflow complete despite unfinished work. Start had also written a folder alias into the feature status field, which the newly enforced continuation validator rejected. The dashboard incorrectly mapped that runtime artifact error to missing Deep-Dive preparation.
records.causalChain: One model session owned the complete autonomous chain -> model returned at a partial boundary -> zero exit was recorded as workflow completion -> saved folder alias failed strict status validation on Continue -> generic readiness messaging prescribed an unrelated Deep Dive
records.testGap: Unit checks covered dispatch and refinement admission but did not execute a full scanner/validator/SQLite workflow through partial returns, new sessions, lifecycle moves, supervised boundaries, cancellation, and finalization. No test paired a known folder alias with dashboard continuation or required recovery text to reflect the actual validation reason.
records.missingDecision: HEPHA must own the outer workflow, dispatch bounded sessions, and evaluate durable evidence after every return. Only explicit autonomy authorizes subsequent phases. A normal worker exit can yield progress, block, or fail; it cannot independently declare the user workflow complete. The document header uses one canonical status vocabulary with a closed legacy alias map, and runtime validation failures have implementation recovery messages.

records.summary: Declare project-owned verification commands during refinement and maintain them during development
records.whyHappened: A valid build regenerated a tracked output and the generic repository fingerprint rejected otherwise passing verification.
records.causalChain: Commands lacked an explicit generated-output and preparation handoff; fingerprinting could not distinguish generation from source edits.
records.testGap: Prompt tests did not establish a common project-owned command inventory across planning and implementation.
records.missingDecision: FeatureDescription owns the TestPlan; refinement discovers configuration statically, developers validate and maintain declarations, Phase files reference check IDs. Runtime freshness handling remains separate work.

records.summary: Refresh publishes corrected command inventories before verification baselines
records.whyHappened: Inspection could correct runtime commands but left stale commands in feature documents, causing later runs to rediscover the same mismatch.
records.causalChain: Read-only inspection selected current configuration -> corrected plan stayed run-local -> persistent TestPlan and Phase references stayed stale.
records.testGap: No end-to-end proof that documented command corrections precede snapshot capture and preserve required behavior and human evidence.
records.missingDecision: An explicit Refresh authorizes bounded host-owned command publication. The model proposes schema-validated command literals; the host preserves protected document content, audits updates, captures the new baseline and strips one-time patches from reusable plans. Generated-output snapshot semantics remain separate work.

records.summary: Recover receipt validation defects before acceptance coverage assessment
records.whyHappened: Passing native results were rejected because the recorded invocation had equivalent literal quoting and console capture. The refresh stopped before coverage assessment.
records.causalChain: Execution succeeds -> importer rejects receipt representation -> application throws immediately -> no agent correction or coverage assessment.
records.testGap: Existing evidence tests established rejection but did not require the owning Refresh to return diagnostics to the agent and continue after a substantiated correction.
records.missingDecision: Evidence validation is a repair boundary, not an unconditional terminal transition. Preserve required scope, current source, native outcome validation and cancellation; reuse valid current-run results. Detect recurring validation defects independent of audit metadata and request diagnosis before escalation.

records.summary: Resume recoverable readiness workers and continue correcting distinct plan and coverage defects
records.whyHappened: Receipt correction existed, but worker errors could bypass it and fixed plan/coverage correction counts stopped otherwise progressing verification.
records.causalChain: Recoverable worker error escapes before receipt import or distinct validation failures exhaust a fixed retry count -> completed work remains saved but the user must restart Refresh.
records.testGap: No process-backed Refresh test covered a worker failing after native results were saved or a correction itself failing. Plan and assessment tests asserted fixed retry counts instead of meaningful progress.
records.missingDecision: Retry with original scope, saved artifacts and the exact failure. Use one shared repeated-diagnostic policy for plan, worker, receipt and coverage correction. Preserve runtime/authority guards, native result validation and current-source binding. Substantive production repair and source changes are not evidence-format recovery.

records.summary: Accept equivalent literal command quoting directly at receipt binding
records.whyHappened: Command text equality and capture prefix matching rejected equivalent quoted arguments after passing test execution.
records.causalChain: Literal quoting differs -> receipt binding rejects valid invocation -> coverage never starts or requests needless model repair.
records.testGap: Earlier recovery tests repaired harmless quoting instead of requiring direct import. No argument-equivalence regression used real shell execution.
records.missingDecision: Compare literal shell words and operators, preserving argument boundaries, assignment syntax, redirection descriptors/order and independently bound logs. Do not execute or guess expansions. Keep the actual receipt unchanged and use native reports to establish test results.

records.summary: Expose manual result actions at the top and separate current case recording from coverage readiness
records.whyHappened: Footer actions disappeared for stale or coverage-incomplete packs, leaving users unable to find the all-pass operation or understand incomplete regeneration. Aggregate review/result admission incorrectly required full coverage although individual valid cases were actionable.
records.causalChain: Incomplete coverage -> whole-pack controls hidden and server rejects recording -> user cannot attest completed manual tests. Paused generation continues displaying the old pack without a prominent explanation.
records.testGap: Prior tests asserted absent buttons and rejected bulk recording instead of preserving per-case evidence independently of coverage.
records.missingDecision: Keep top actions visible with explicit unavailable reasons. Permit review and all-pass recording for current validated manual cases; retain version/review/failed-result guards and never grant completion for unresolved coverage.

records.summary: Recover manual authoring drafts and assess independent evidence without presentation or metadata layout coupling
records.whyHappened: A fixed first-verb rule rejected concrete manual instructions, malformed drafts stopped generation immediately, stale manual packs suppressed automated assessment, and introductory sections hid existing lifecycle metadata. Recovery UI children also implicitly occupied the title/status grid columns.
records.causalChain: Valid test execution -> unrelated manual/artifact prerequisite suppresses coverage -> regeneration rejects draft without correction -> old pack remains displayed and cannot be reviewed. Additional recovery elements squeeze phase titles instead of occupying their own full-width rows.
records.testGap: No regression covered correcting rejected manual drafts in one operation, assessing current evidence with a stale or absent manual pack, relocated metadata identity or real browser geometry with simultaneous artifact and coverage gaps.
records.missingDecision: Treat invalid model proposals as recoverable input under the same contract; retain validated batches and stop repeated no-progress or ownership/source changes. Assess current evidence independently while keeping completion/human review guards. Document identity selects lifecycle metadata; phase identity never selects gates. Recovery UI children span full width except the explicitly placed title and status.

records.summary: Make explicit phase investigation repair confirmed findings and verify changed source automatically
records.whyHappened: Any investigation gap forced the entire repair into an inspection-only prompt and dropped other unresolved findings. Saved instructions repeated that restriction. A report-only phase edit then invalidated fresh evidence and automatic reassessment stopped.
records.causalChain: Explicit repair -> investigation-only filtering and prompt -> another report without corrections -> changed feature fingerprint -> manual refresh dead end.
records.testGap: The prior regression required inspection-only behavior. No test covered a mixed repair request or automatic fresh verification after a completed repair changed source.
records.missingDecision: Explicit repair authorizes investigation, confirmed in-scope correction and affected verification within one bounded invocation. Preserve all unresolved findings, prerequisites, valid evidence and human acceptance; follow changed-source reassessment into fresh verification with cancellation/successor guards.

records.summary: Share logical acceptance assessment and keep numeric instrumentation optional
records.whyHappened: The automatic phase gate used structured logical assertion mappings while readiness saw only Markdown/execution context. Legacy refinement/profile policy still introduced mandatory numeric coverage, and the fixer requested clarification for a missing measurement policy.
records.causalChain: Existing integration assertions and passing runs -> logical phase assessment -> structured mappings omitted at feature assessment -> unnecessary investigation. Separately, no numeric tooling -> role-derived LCOV prerequisite despite acceptance coverage being logical.
records.testGap: No regression passed the same phase assertion mappings/current source into readiness without numeric reports or validated a final profile without a coverage intent. Repair authority was not varied across phase identities.
records.missingDecision: Assess logical FEAT/EPIC behavior collectively using current tests and prior source-backed mappings; execution remains independently verified. Optional numeric telemetry cannot introduce a gate. Refresh does not create tests or fix code; explicit phase repair does, generically.

records.summary: Separate test source ownership from execution identity and preserve readiness recovery diagnostics
records.whyHappened: Independent filtered scenario groups shared source files. The validator rejected file overlap as duplicate execution, then restricted a correction to the diagnostic prefix rather than both named participants. The correction timed out and only the runtime route error reached readiness.
records.causalChain: Valid filtered commands -> shared-file rejection -> partial correction scope rejection -> runtime timeout before execution -> readiness blocked without its original diagnostic.
records.testGap: Prior tests required file-overlap rejection instead of executing independent scenarios from shared files. Correction tests covered only one diagnosed check and did not assert retained root cause after a runtime failure.
records.missingDecision: Source identity cannot prove runtime selection identity. Preserve all test references; reject exact duplicate executions, inspect delegated selections, permit both conflict participants in corrections, and retain the cause and explicit readiness retry path without bypassing runtime limits.

records.summary: Generate and enforce a shared execution receipt exchange and bind output paths deterministically
records.whyHappened: Portable command inventory placeholders reached execution and receipt binding unresolved. Workers expanded the path correctly but the importer rejected the receipt. The receipt prompt also maintained an independent handwritten JSON example.
records.causalChain: Portable output placeholder -> correct execution with absolute paths -> unresolved command comparison -> unnecessary model evidence repair -> stalled readiness before logical assessment.
records.testGap: No test combined portable output placeholders with expanded native receipt bindings, a host-owned template and the same schema used by both sender and receiver.
records.missingDecision: Host owns immutable identities and output binding. The model fills a versioned schema; native execution facts remain independently verified. Representation normalization cannot require repeated passing tests or create acceptance. Explicitly separate checksum-bound supporting artifacts from native test reports; never relabel arbitrary invalid reports automatically.

records.summary: Verify completion against accepted feature scope without introducing new requirements
records.whyHappened: Completion assessment treated additional test depth, unrelated parent criteria and old manual authoring notes as new gates, while another confirmation click separated recognized evidence from readiness.
records.causalChain: Broad sufficiency question -> stronger requirements and missing-context findings -> repair or regeneration loops -> passing accepted feature remains blocked.
records.testGap: Missing coverage for collective accepted verification, future proposals, baseline identity, automatic semantic links and scoped post-repair reassessment.
records.missingDecision: Planning owns scope. Execution and completion verify it. Extra work requires future planning authority. Invalid or incomplete assessment is recoverable operational work, never a new requirement or fabricated pass.

records.summary: Accept equivalent report bindings and resume interrupted validation from current evidence
records.whyHappened: A native stdout file used as both report and audit log was rejected as duplicate execution; legitimate multi-repository qualifications only accepted one spelling. Recovery stalled while searching outside its bounded evidence scope.
records.causalChain: Valid tests -> receipt representation rejection -> broad recovery search timeout -> refresh repeated already passing execution.
records.testGap: Missing native/audit alias, multi-repository hash-first wording, and explicit-refresh validation-resume tests.
records.missingDecision: Count native evidence once, validate all configured source owners, and independently revalidate interrupted evidence before resuming assessment. Do not infer new execution or human acceptance.

records.summary: Separate automated feature acceptance from required manual acknowledgement
records.whyHappened: Readiness consumed manual package coverage classifications and required reviewed manual PASS links as criterion evidence.
records.causalChain: Manual results entered logical assessment -> model returned manual contribution -> result-binding rejection prevented automated acceptance.
records.testGap: No regression separated human acknowledgement from automated criterion evidence and cache freshness.
records.missingDecision: Acceptance links use automated assertions only. Manual acknowledgement remains independent and required; manual-only obligations stay outside automated scope.

records.summary: Preserve accumulated assertion evidence while recovering pending acceptance decisions
records.whyHappened: Each retrieval assessment restarted from the original prompt and only appended the newest files. Two-hop cutoff and unresolved document anchors also prevented available source from reaching the assessor.
records.causalChain: Passing execution -> missing source request -> source retrieved -> next retry discards earlier source -> evidence remains pending despite locally available assertions.
records.testGap: Single-helper recovery had no multi-hop, retained-decision or feature-document-anchor regression.
records.missingDecision: Readiness must accumulate requested source, retain validated decisions and follow new references within bounded context and spending. The accepted report defines the collective verification approach. Unavailable context never establishes a missing implementation or a pass.

records.summary: Close the repair/verification loop and recover verification-generated source drift
records.whyHappened: A successful configured build rewrote a tracked generated declaration. The host rejected the changed aggregate snapshot without diagnosing filenames or entering setup recovery. Separately, an unknown historical health summary overwrote a newer linked repair decision.
records.causalChain: build regenerates tracked output -> source fingerprint differs -> unconditional stop before logical assessment -> browser user repeatedly refreshes without recovery context.
records.testGap: Freshness tests only expected source drift to stop. They did not exercise a process whose output settles after configuration inspection and another execution, repeated drift, or cancellation inside recovery.
records.missingDecision: Reject the stale attempt while continuing owned recovery. Keep real source checks; re-inspect with changed-file evidence and rerun all checks under a new baseline. Bound continuous drift and expose browser retry. Preserve linked explicit health repair evidence over unknown prose, while retaining observed failures. A selected phase repair must verify its postcondition and feed concrete unresolved evidence into subsequent attempts. After three unsuccessful rounds, report per-round work claimed, independent verification and specific remaining diagnostics, with the phase textbox available for another user-steered loop.

records.summary: Keep compatibility MCP tool identity independent of model and display-prefix configuration
records.whyHappened: The prompt normalized the server prefix and instructed the worker to call an identifier the gateway did not advertise.
records.causalChain: Synthesized display alias -> tool lookup fails -> no recipe execution -> unchanged lifecycle evidence.
records.testGap: Existing prompt tests repeated the incorrect alias and did not execute the rendered invocation against a server-scoped tool catalog. Review also identified that a gateway fixture alone assumes external resolver behavior; the repeatable installed-adapter contract check now verifies that boundary.
records.missingDecision: Use exact original tool identity with an explicit server selector. Prefix formatting belongs to the gateway, never a model/provider branch. Preserve response validation, workflow modes and existing failure and retry policy.

records.summary: Delegate MCP recipe policy to the returned instructions instead of duplicating it in the launch prompt
records.whyHappened: The compatibility launcher composed shared native verification and acceptance prose with a full phase-gate schema even though the MCP response already supplies them.
records.causalChain: Native policy injection plus recipe policy plus repeated schema -> larger startup context and competing procedural instructions.
records.testGap: Prompt tests required copied policy strings and did not check the complete implementation launch for duplicate schema or instructions.
records.missingDecision: MCP owns procedural instructions. HEPHA launch metadata supplies routing, current diagnostics, session authority and local integration paths; host validation remains deterministic. Host-directed repair without a recipe response retains its own contract.

records.summary: Enforce MCP refinement decision boundaries and exercise returned gate-schema interoperability
records.whyHappened: Prompt de-duplication exposed a refinement decision boundary that was only expressed in worker instructions; existing launch tests did not exercise the returned gate schema.
records.causalChain: Unresolved target decisions plus provider Ready projection could produce false refinement completion; incompatible wire records could otherwise go unnoticed in prompt-only tests.
records.testGap: No refusal-before-dispatch test, no Ready-with-unresolved-decisions result test, and no independent returned MCP schema-to-published-record lifecycle fixture.
records.missingDecision: Enforce target decisions at host admission and completion. Validate independent provider schema compatibility and actual record admission without restoring policy duplication or inferring applicability from phase identity.

records.summary: Move hosted Deep-Dive procedures into MCP and remove native workflow skill injection from MCP workers
records.whyHappened: Deep-Dive retained its own native interview procedures while the delivery calls used MCP. MCP delivery workers also exposed native workflow skill/template discovery.
records.causalChain: Two procedural authorities -> repeated context or conflicting workflow selection; a full interactive MCP recipe cannot safely replace one hosted UI turn.
records.testGap: No cross-boundary coverage for hosted MCP opening/follow-up/chat/apply-answers stages, one-copy context, cancellation during retrieval, malformed follow-up closure, or recipe-source isolation of workflow skills.
records.missingDecision: Define bounded hosted stages in MCP. Fetch and validate the selected contract, then run Pi without tools using procedure plus saved data once. Keep UI/storage/routing/admission in HEPHA. Recipe failure cannot synthesize a native result.

records.summary: Preserve current interview context and source content across MCP responses
records.whyHappened: Review found that the initial hosted context omitted fresh primary content, follow-up design constraints and earlier chat decisions. Unvalidated full rewrites could erase source, and HTTP limits were applied after buffering.
records.causalChain: Stale/incomplete context -> conflicting model decisions; empty or partial rewrites -> destructive source replacement; late response limits -> avoidable memory use.
records.testGap: Initial tests used unchanged primary content, one question and short successful responses. They did not exercise intervening edits, truncated output, conflicting anchors or streamed oversized bodies.
records.missingDecision: Use current preparation snapshots and complete saved decisions; publish versioned exact edits against the snapshot; validate shape, uniqueness and overlap before applying; refuse a source changed during execution; enforce transport byte limits while reading and cancel oversized streams.
